Title: Borders secure despite foreign settlement reports – Saifuddin
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: Malaysia's borders remain secure against all forms of threats, including foreign infiltration, smuggling and human trafficking, says Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said border security remained a government priority amid reports in neighbouring countries' media about attempts by foreign elements to establish settlements near Malaysia's borders.
"There have been reports, widely covered by media in our neighbouring country, about attempts to build settlements involving foreign elements along our border.
"However, our priority is to ensure the security of our borders against all forms of threats.
"Whether it is the infiltration of foreign elements, smuggling or human trafficking, we will ensure that our border areas remain secure. That is our priority," he said.
Saifuddin said the government would not single out any particular threat, given the complex and dynamic nature of border management.
"I do not want to pinpoint what form of threat it is.
"Managing a border that is so complex and dynamic requires us to look at security from a comprehensive perspective.
"We do not look at it in isolation or separately just because of one or two incidents that have occurred. That is our approach," he said.
He said all relevant enforcement agencies would continue to ensure Malaysia's borders remained secure against any potential threats.
Saifuddin said the comprehensive approach was necessary to ensure the country's security measures remained effective in dealing with evolving threats along its borders.
He said this after handing over the RM80.1 million Third Region Marine Police Base project in Tok Bali here today.
Also present were Federal Internal Security and Public Order director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.

Title: Increase in special draws a collective responsibility of previous government, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decision to increase the number of special draw days for forecast numbers to 22 times a year during the previous administration was a collective responsibility of the government at the time, including ministers from Pas, said Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
Tengku Zafrul, who is now the Senior Political Adviser to the Prime Minister, said special draws were not new, having been introduced in 1999, while the ceiling of 22 draws a year already existed during the Barisan Nasional administration before he was appointed Finance Minister.
"During the (Covid-19) pandemic, the government at the time returned to the existing ceiling of 22 draws a year, and this matter was also conveyed to Parliament through an official reply.
"Importantly, under today's Madani government, the number of special draws has been reduced to just eight times a year," he said.
Tengku Zafrul said this in response to certain parties who had sought to pin responsibility for the decision to increase the number of special draws on him personally.
He added that the facts surrounding the issue were clear and that he had no intention of prolonging a polemic that could distract the government from its national development agenda.
"The focus of the Madani government is to solve the people's problems and ensure that every policy genuinely benefits them," he said.
The issue of special forecast number draws was raised again following claims and disputes over the justification for increasing the number of draws during the Covid-19 pandemic.
After taking over the administration in December 2022, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that the number of special draws would be reduced from 22 to eight times a year, starting in 2023.

Title: Anwar: Indian community will not be sidelined
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Madani government will continue to expand financing opportunities for Indian entrepreneurs and strengthen the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra).
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would also step up entrepreneurship and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programmes, while creating more opportunities for youth development through mentor-mentee programmes.
He said various initiatives had been implemented in education, entrepreneurship, microfinancing, welfare and cash assistance to ease families' burdens and improve their standard of living.
"Continuing a series of engagements with Indian community leaders to assess the progress of the Madani government's agenda, as well as hear their views and concerns, I emphasised that the Indian community will never be sidelined.
"The Madani government will continue to expand access to financing for entrepreneurs, strengthen Mitra, enhance entrepreneurship and TVET training, and create more opportunities for youth development through mentor-mentee programmes," he said in a social media post today.
Anwar also called on relevant ministries and agencies to strengthen coordination and improve service delivery to ensure every allocation and policy reaches its intended recipients and brings tangible improvements to their lives.
He said existing gaps, particularly those involving poverty, citizenship and access to assistance, must be addressed promptly and effectively.

Title: High Court dismisses union's judicial review, affirms DG's powers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Kuala Lumpur High Court has upheld the Director‑General of Trade Unions' (KPKS) authority, dismissing a judicial review by a waste management union and affirming that the DG acted lawfully under the Trade Unions Act 1959.
The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) said the ruling confirmed the statutory powers and duties of the KPKS in regulating trade union governance.
"Specifically, it ensures that trade union affairs and governance are carried out in line with legal requirements," the ministry said in a statement.
The judicial review was filed by the Peninsular Malaysia Maintenance Services and Waste Management Workers Union after the director-general's May 9, 2024 decision refusing to register Kamarul Baharin Mansor as union secretary for the 2023/2026 term due to employment status issues.
The dispute centred on whether Kamarul Baharin qualified as a "workman" under Section 26(1A) of the Act.
The court dismissed the application and ordered the union to pay RM5,000 in costs, ruling that the director-general acted lawfully under investigative powers provided by Section 4A.
According to Kesuma, the decision affirms the director-general's powers to determine eligibility for union membership and office, clarifying that freedom of association must operate within the legal framework.
"The right of workers to form, join and participate in trade unions remains respected and protected, provided conditions and qualifications set by law are met," the ministry said.
Kesuma added it will continue strengthening freedom of association and good governance, stressing that the rule of law underpins workers' rights and ensures a fair, orderly and harmonious labour ecosystem.– BERNAMA

Title: Police make new arrests over Malaysian pilot's drug smuggling case
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: Police have made several new arrests to assist in the investigation into a Malaysian pilot who was detained by Indonesian authorities for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs worth RM45 million.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said swift action by the
Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department
had led to several new arrests in the case.
"The department is also cooperating with the authorities of the neighbouring country," he said.
He said this after attending the handover ceremony for the Tok Bali Marine Police Region Three headquarters project here today.
In July, a 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was
detained
at the International Arrivals Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten, after arriving from Kuala Lumpur on flight MH727.
He was detained about 11.30pm local time after Indonesian customs officers detected suspicious luggage belonging to the pilot through an X-ray scan before directing him to the examination room after he had claimed the luggage.
Further inspection found 14 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills weighing about 25kg in the luggage, as well as four grammes of methamphetamine in his hand luggage, with the drugs estimated to be worth RM45 million.
According to Indonesian police, the pilot had allegedly been promised RM50,000 to transport the drugs to Jakarta before they were to be collected by another individual at a hotel.

Title: Haze: API readings drop at six Sabah stations, four remain unhealthy
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Air quality in Sabah showed signs of improvement today, with six monitoring stations recording lower Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm compared to yesterday, though four stations remained at unhealthy levels.
The most significant decrease was in Sandakan, where the API dropped to 93 from 151, returning to the moderate category. Tawau also improved, falling to 98 from 103 yesterday.
Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 156 compared to 176, Keningau dropped to 153 from 174, Kota Kinabalu eased to 156 from 171, while Kimanis fell to 154 from 170.
The Sabah Department of Environment (DOE) said no major fire incidents were detected around Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Papar, Beaufort, Sandakan and Tawau, based on reports from the Sabah Fire and Rescue Department and DOE patrols.
Satellite imagery from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed no hotspots in Sabah yesterday. However, 780 active hotspots were detected in Kalimantan and 142 in Sumatra on Sept 2.
DOE said it remains prepared to step up enforcement and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, with 502 Open Burning Prevention Operation (OMPT) patrols carried out to date.
The public is advised against open burning and urged to monitor the latest API readings via the DOE website or the official MyJAS EQMS application.– BERNAMA

Title: Niche Capital Emas' development partner receives license for rare earth extraction's chemicals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Niche Capital Emas Holdings Bhd's joint development partner Greensnow Consolidated Bhd has received an interim manufacturing licence from the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry to manufacture green chemical and bio-based solvents for rare earth extraction in Kuantan.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Niche Capital said that the licence was given to Greensnow Biosolution Sdn Bhd, a unit of Greensnow on Aug 9.
Among the terms and conditions set out under the licence include maintaining capital investment per employee of not less than RM140,000.
Greensnow must also ensure that at least 80 per cent of its workforce is Malaysian.
Niche Capital added that Greensnow is required to submit the relevant supporting documents to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority within six months from the date of the approval letter in order to facilitate the issuance of the full licence.
"Securing this approval aligns closely with Malaysia's current industrial policy objectives. By establishing an integrated end-to-end rare earth value chain, the initiative supports the nation's strategy to promote domestic value creation and strengthen its midstream and downstream rare earth industries through higher value-added processing and manufacturing activities," it said.
Niche Capital's share price closed unchanged at nine sen on Thursday, valuing the company at RM157.13 million.

Title: Caruana Galizia: 'One-woman WikiLeaks' who exposed Malta's shady side
Article:
ILLICIT trafficking, bribes, offshore accounts: Maltese journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, murdered with a car bomb in 2017, fearlessly exposed corruption in her archipelago in the heart of the Mediterranean.
In the final entry on her blog, posted barely half an hour before she was killed, Caruana Galizia wrote:
"There are crooks everywhere you look now. The situation is desperate."
Nearly nine years on, the Maltese justice system has still not determined who ordered the murder of the investigative journalist.
Five men have been convicted of supplying the explosives and carrying out the killing.
On Wednesday, Maltese tycoon Yorgen Fenech, who had been accused of masterminding it, was acquitted by a court in Valletta.
The businessman was arrested at the end of 2019 on board his yacht as he tried to leave Malta.
According to the indictment, he had ordered the journalist's murder because she was about to publish a compromising article about a family member.
[[nid:1525144]]
'Poison pen'
Born on Aug 26, 1964, Caruana Galizia had worked as a columnist for several Maltese media outlets, including The Sunday Times of Malta and The Malta Independent.
But it was above all through her blog, Running Commentary, followed by some 400,000 readers on an island with half a million inhabitants, that she became known far beyond Malta.
Dubbed the "one-woman WikiLeaks", she never gave in to attempts at intimidation.
She was survived by her husband and three sons, who have fought for justice for years.
Her biting, uncompromising style earned her the label of "poison-pen writer" from her critics.
In Malta, home to 70,000 offshore companies and the headquarters of some of the world's largest gambling groups, she wielded her pen against ministers and businessmen.
The mass of documents she left behind was taken up by 45 journalists from 18 media outlets brought together in the "Daphne Project" – one of the first initiatives of the NGO Forbidden Stories, which continues the investigations of journalists who have been silenced.
Her assassination exposed corruption at the highest levels of the state and triggered a political crisis, forcing then prime minister Joseph Muscat to resign in 2020.
Muscat was accused of having interfered in and protected associates during the investigation into the journalist's murder.
The crisis did not prevent Muscat's Labour Party from remaining in power: his successor Robert Abela was comfortably re-elected earlier this year.
* The article is from AFP

Title: Outrage mounts in Malta after acquittal over journalist's murder
Article:
VALLETTA: Hundreds of people demonstrated in the Maltese capital Valletta after a wealthy businessman was found not guilty of masterminding the murder of an investigative journalist.
The verdict on Daphne Caruana Galizia's car-bomb killing in 2017 sparked outrage from Maltese civil society groups and international media freedom organisations.
The opposition Nationalist Party, which organised the demonstration late on Wednesday, has said lawmakers should be called back from their summer break for a special session of the legislature to discuss the case.
Hours earlier, tycoon Yorgen Fenech walked out of court after the verdict as a free man to shouts of "Assassin!" from some protesters.
Five people have been convicted so far in relation to the murder for supplying the explosives and carrying out the killing.
The Committee to Protect Journalists in a statement on Thursday said it would continue to "seek accountability for all those involved in her murder."
The European Centre for Press and Media Freedom said the verdict sent a "disturbing message", while Reporters Without Borders (RSF), another media watchdog, said it was "beyond outraged."
"The verdict means that almost nine years since the assassination of Daphne Caruana Galizia, the Maltese authorities have failed to identify and convict the mastermind," RSF said in a statement.
"Full justice must be served and Maltese authorities must implement the long overdue measures protecting journalists and media freedom."
The government on Wednesday said it "took note" of the verdict and appealed for "prudence in public comments" on the case.
Dubbed a "one-woman WikiLeaks", Caruana Galizia exposed corruption at the highest level in the country, shining a spotlight on murky links between Malta's business and political elites.
Her slaying put Malta, the European Union's smallest member state, in the spotlight over its apparent rule-of-law failings.
The killing also led to a political crisis, and the resignation of then-premier Joseph Muscat in January 2020 after widespread anger and mass protests over his perceived efforts to protect friends and allies from the investigation.
A two-year public inquiry published in July 2021 concluded that the state should "shoulder responsibility" for the murder due to the "atmosphere of impunity" the government had created.
Fenech, a tycoon whose business interests spanned the energy and tourism sectors, was arrested on his yacht in 2019 as he tried to sail out of Malta after a middleman in the murder was offered a pardon to identify those involved.
Prosecutors had accused Fenech of ordering the journalist to be killed because she was on the brink of publishing a compromising article about his uncle.
Caruana Galizia was 53 when she died and left behind a husband and three sons.
In June 2025, Robert Agius and Jamie Vella were convicted of supplying the bomb that killed her and sentenced to life in prison.
The three men who carried out the murder – brothers George and Alfred Degiorgio together with Vince Muscat – are serving prison sentences after being found guilty of their role.
"Accountability is now overdue for all those who enabled, facilitated, or protected her murderers," her family said in a statement on Tuesday.
"Nine years after Daphne's brutal assassination, the institutional failures that enabled her murder remain unaddressed and unreformed."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends marginally higher as BNM maintains OPR, sees resilient growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended marginally higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) maintaining the overnight policy rate (OPR).
The Malaysian central bank also assessed that the current monetary policy stance remains consistent with the outlook for continued price stability and sustainable economic growth.
At 6pm, the ringgit was quoted at 4.0405/0445 against the US dollar compared with Wednesday's close of 4.0435/0475.
BNM maintained the OPR at 2.75 per cent at its meeting today, noting that economic indicators point to resilient global growth, supported by strong global technology expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labour markets.
It said solid growth momentum is expected to bring Malaysia's economic growth to around five per cent in 2026, while the economy's sound fundamentals are expected to keep growth resilient in 2027.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the ringgit remained in a tight range against the greenback as markets awaited the US non-farm payrolls (NFP) figures to be released on Friday night.
"Thus far, the ADP Employment Report has fallen short of expectations, with private-sector employment increasing by only 38,000 in August, signalling that the NFP could potentially disappoint market expectations. At the moment, the markets are spooked by the hawkish statement from the US Federal Reserve chairman last week. Hence, the incoming data will dictate the evolving market sentiment," he told Bernama.
Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit dipped against the euro to 4.6894/6940 from 4.6787/6834 yesterday and eased against the British pound to 5.4539/4593 from 5.4527/4581.
The local note also weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5838/5865 from 2.5294/5321 at Wednesday's close.
The ringgit traded mostly lower against regional currencies.
It was flat against the Philippine peso at 6.46/6.47 since yesterday and declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1850/1884 from 3.1739/1773.
It fell against the Thai baht to 12.2421/2598 from 12.1321/1488 and also traded lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 228.5/228.8 from 227.6/227.9 at yesterday's close.

Title: Businessman: I'm not that "poor and lowly" to use Muhyiddin's name
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman told the High Court here today that he was neither a bad person nor "so poor and lowly" that he was desperate enough to use the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's name to obtain money for Bersatu.
The 27th prosecution witness, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, said he was only indebted to the former prime minister for helping Bumiputera contractors through the implementation of projects under the Jana Ekonomi Pemerkasaan Kontraktor Bumiputera Berwibawa (Jana Wibawa) programme during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Azman, who is also Malaysian Bumiputera Contractors Association president, said he came to court only to give truthful testimony after taking his oath as a witness.
"I came to court to tell the truth. I do not care whether Tan Sri Muhyiddin wins or loses this case.
"What is important is that I am here to tell the truth and I have already taken my oath," he said.
During re-examination, Deputy Public Prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin also questioned Azman's position that he did not agree that he had received special treatment despite having been investigated for the serious offences of soliciting and receiving bribes.
When asked what was meant by special treatment, Azman said it was for the court to determine.
Wan Shaharuddin: Why do you disagree that, despite being investigated for the serious offences of soliciting and receiving bribes, you were given "special treatment"?
Azman: What did the lawyer mean by special treatment? Is it because I was not charged or remanded that this constitutes special treatment? It is for the judge to evaluate.
Azman was also referred to a complaint form prepared during an investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
He said he disagreed with the contents of the form, which stated that he had solicited and received money from companies linked to the procurement of Jana Wibawa projects.
Azman said that during a meeting with Muhyiddin at a golf event in July 2020, he was informed that if anyone intended to make a contribution to Bersatu, it should be deposited directly into the party's account and not given to an individual.
He said that although he knew the Bersatu president's actions were wrong, he did not lodge a report on the contribution to Bersatu at Muhyiddin's request.
"Corruption involves those who have power. I have no power to award projects to any company because that power lies with the Prime Minister and the Finance Ministry," he said.
When asked whether he had "opened the door" for a company director known as TC Lian, Azman explained that he had merely introduced the businessman to an individual known as Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad.
"Adam Radlan has nothing to do with this case. Adam Radlan was like a postman, merely making the connection with Lian," he said.
Meanwhile, at the end of the re-examination, High Court judge Datuk Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin asked Azman whether he was still active in any political party.
Judge: I just want to know whether you are still a member of any political party.
Azman: I am still a member of Umno.
Muhyiddin, 79, faces four charges of using his position to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for Bersatu from Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd, Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Mamfor Sdn Bhd, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Azman, in connection with Jana Wibawa projects.
He is also facing three charges of receiving RM200 million in proceeds from unlawful activities from Bukhary Equity, which were deposited into Bersatu's AmBank and CIMB Bank accounts in Petaling Jaya and Kuala Lumpur between February 2021 and July 2022.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gaza seed bank helps farmers cultivate the little land they have left
Article:
A group of farmers has been working to preserve Gaza's native crops by rebuilding a local seed bank that was destroyed during Israel's war in the enclave and by encouraging Palestinians to cultivate what little viable land they have left.
Most of Gaza's pre-war farmland lies in an area under Israeli military occupation.
Gaza's entire two million population is penned into around 30 per cent of the tiny enclave, much of which was laid to waste by two years of Israeli bombardment.
That includes Gaza farmer Salama Muhanna's "Bank of Seeds", which he says was destroyed in Qarara town, south of the enclave, in early 2024, several months after the Hamas-led attacks that precipitated Israel's military assault.
Before the war, Muhanna said, "we had refrigerators, solar power, a dryer, a seed-cleaning and sorting machine - we had everything."
The bank had once held 70 tonnes of stocks for 42 different crops, including black-eyed peas, watermelon and sage, all staples of Palestinian agricultural heritage, he said.
Muhanna, 71, said he and his team of farmers have rebuilt a modest stock of some 32 local seeds in recent months, through contributions from farmers who worked with the bank before the war.
The seeds are carefully arranged in burlap sacks and plastic containers in a makeshift tent now in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip. He and his team also cultivate seedlings in fields surrounding the tent.
Local heirloom seeds are more resilient than hybrid varieties available for import, Muhanna said, as they can be saved and replanted year after year.
The Israeli military did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Farmers see local seed banks as protection against border closures and supply restrictions, but say they do little to offset the devastation of Gaza's agricultural sector, once a backbone of the economy.
[[nid:1525123]]
According to a June report by Gaza's Agriculture Ministry, about 560,000 people depended wholly or partly on agriculture and fishing for their livelihoods before the war.
"What is being done through the seed bank, and the seeds currently available, represents only a drop in the ocean compared with the needs facing the agricultural sector," said Osama Al-Mukhalalati, an agricultural engineer with the International Committee of the Red Cross.
Mustafa Al-Astal, who runs a nursery in southern Gaza's Khan Younis, said local seeds had become "the only lifeline" when Israel tightened import restrictions and humanitarian aid flows during 2025.
Israel said that measure was aimed at pressuring the militant group Hamas during ceasefire talks.
It was condemned by Palestinians and rights groups as a form of collective punishment, and a global hunger monitor said it set off famine in parts of Gaza.
Much of Gaza's farmland lies along and beyond the "Yellow Line" to which Israeli troops were meant to withdraw under an October 2025 Israel-Hamas ceasefire.
Reuters has reported that Israel has unilaterally moved the concrete blocks marking the Yellow Line on the ground deeper into Hamas-controlled territory.
Local farmers say this has put even more viable farmland off limits, and exposed those who tend areas near it to Israeli gunfire.
Khaled Al-Astal, a Palestinian farmer who has been planting seeds from Muhanna's seed bank in an area 500 metres from the Yellow Line, said he and other farmers have no plans to leave the area, despite the danger of Israeli attacks.
"We only have about 25 to 30 per cent left (of Gaza). So we say: we are here on our land, and we will cultivate it despite them."
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Proton records highest monthly domestic sales in August, YTD up 40pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Proton Holdings Bhd recorded the highest monthly domestic sales volume in August, with total sales of 22,632 units, as Proton e.MAS chalked another record-setting month, while demand for internal combustion engine (ICE) remains strong.
The national automotive company on Thursday said that its cumulative sales for the first eight months of 2026 stood at 141,421 units, 40.2 per cent higher year-on-year. Based on the forecast total industry volume, the cumulative sales number translates into a market share of 25.6 per cent year-to-date (YTD).
The Proton S70 has seen an upturn in popularity since the introduction of the updated 2026 model in February, resulting in a new all-time volume high-point for the model last month.
A total of 3,235 units were delivered to Malaysian customers in August to bring the model's YTD total to 17,953 units, placing it ahead of its total volume from 2025 with four months remaining this year.
Similarly, the company's SUV models continue to lead their segments. The Proton X50 remains the B-segment SUV category YTD sales leader and Malaysia's best-selling SUV.
A total of 2,274 units were sold in August to keep sales ahead of last year's performance.
Similarly, the Proton X90 remains the leader for seven-seater D-segment SUVs, with 471 units delivered in August. According to Proton, the model is now 64 per cent ahead of its 2025 achievement.
Meanwhile, the Proton Saga remains a favourite with Proton fans, achieving 7,347 units sold in August. Its YTD number is now just shy of 60,000 units keeping it 33.3 per cent ahead of last year and on target to exceed an annual sales volume of 80,000 units.
Proton deputy chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Abdul Rashid Musa said the company has reached an important milestone that reflects the confidence customers place in its products and services.
"Our range continues to offer technology, design, quality, safety and performance, supported by a strong value proposition.
"At the same time, we are making strong gains in our export business, particularly in the area of assembling vehicles for our partner Geely, while on-going efforts by the Proton e.MAS team have resulted in the brand taking a dominant market share in the EV market and another record-setting month.
"As a result, Proton is well-placed to reach its year-end volume and financial goals, benefitting the entire local automotive ecosystem as a whole," he said.
Additionally a total of 6,047 units for the e.MAS were delivered last month, setting a new high mark for the electric vehicle (EV) sub-brand. Cumulatively, YTD sales now stand at 27,860 units, with all three models leading their respective segments.
The B-segment e.MAS 5 remains Malaysia's best-selling EV with 4,818 units delivered in August, setting a new national record for monthly volume from a single EV model.
Its C-segment SUV sibling, the Proton e.MAS 7, had 613 units sold while the Proton e.MAS 7 PHEV reached 616 units as local assembly volume started ramping up.
"PRO-NET is humbled by the confidence Malaysians have in Proton e.MAS and our electrical mobility solutions, which is reflected in the continued high demand for all our models," said PRO-NET CEO Zhang Qiang.
"As we continue with efforts to deliver units as quickly as possible, our expansion into areas such as partnering charge point operators to grow charging infrastructure, growing the dealership network and continuing to engage owners on multiple levels ensure we are able to offer a holistic ownership experience making the transition to xEVs a smooth one for all buyers," he added.

Title: KKDW denies unilateral spending claims over rural road projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The rural and regional development ministry (KKDW) has denied allegations that it made unilateral financial commitments or "spent as it pleased" over excess commitments for rural road projects.
KKDW press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil said project approvals and allocations were subject to established government procedures, with the economy ministry responsible for project approval and the finance ministry (MoF) determining allocations.
He said KKDW's role was limited to applying for and holding rural road allocations before channelling them to the Public Works Department (JKR), which is responsible for the technical and procurement processes, including tenders, contractor appointments and payments.
"KKDW does not make commitments unilaterally. JKR is the technical department with the expertise to manage the procurement process.
"KKDW's responsibility is only to bid for and hold the allocation before it is handed over to JKR," he said in a statement.
Fadzmel said 517 new rural road projects worth RM36.6 billion had been approved between 2016 and 2026, while annual allocations from MoF during the same period totalled only about RM12 billion.
He said the approval of new projects was necessary as rural development needs were dynamic and often driven by local economic pressures, geographical factors and urgent post-disaster requirements, including floods.
"Any government in power would still need to approve new projects to meet the critical needs of the people.
"In 2024 alone, 79 new projects worth nearly RM6.9 billion were approved. To date, 415 rural road projects are still being managed, with a total cost exceeding RM34 billion," he said.
Addressing the issue of excess commitments reflected in MOF's expenditure records, Fadzmel said these did not represent new spending but deferred payments carried forward from 2019 to 2021.
"The excess shown is government debt carried forward to subsequent years, not new commitments. KKDW only implements projects according to allocations approved by Parliament," he said.
He cited a hypothetical RM300 million project approved under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP), with an annual ceiling of RM60 million under the Rolling Plan (RP).
He said delays in the tender process during the Covid-19 pandemic could result in RM120 million allocated under RP1 and RP2 being returned to MoF.
However, when work resumed under RP3, contractors could seek payment of the RM120 million in arrears, in addition to the RM60 million allocation for RP3, creating a financial liability carried forward.
Fadzmel said KKDW had also settled outstanding payments to contractors through internal transfers from other rural development programmes before issuing warrants to JKR for payment.
"This occurred when project commitments exceeded the annual cash ceiling provided. However, records show that from 2022 to 2025, rural road projects expenditure remained within the revised allocations available," he said.
He said KKDW did not create the projects independently, but submitted applications which were subject to MoF's budget screening process before allocations were channelled to JKR.
"I hope these four factors can be clearly understood so that the issue is not continuously politicised, leading to misinterpretation of the government's administrative affairs and procedures," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EU lawmakers demand Brussels force Meta to 'protect' European children
Article:
BRUSSELS: European lawmakers demanded that the European Union executive force Meta to change the "addictive" design of its platforms in Europe, as the giant has promised to do in some US states, according to a letter seen by AFP on Thursday.
Meta agreed last month to pay a coalition of US states as much as US$16.7 billion and to impose sweeping new limits on how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram, including an automatic night-time block, as part of a landmark court settlement.
The 27-nation EU has been pushing for similar changes and in July told Meta to change its "addictive design" in findings the company said it disagreed with at the time.
Now in a letter dated Wednesday from French EU lawmaker Stephanie Yon-Courtin and signed by 51 other members of the European Parliament (MEPs) from across the political spectrum, Brussels is urged to act fast and to force Meta's hand.
"European children are worth no less than American ones," the letter said.
"It would therefore be untenable for European minors to end up less well protected, when our framework is the most demanding in the world."
The lawmakers said the European Commission, the EU's digital regulator, should conclude its probe into Meta "without further delay" with a "non-compliance decision" and penalties.
"And should commitments be accepted.., they must on no account fall short of what Meta has just granted to American users," the MEPs said in the letter addressed to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
They also suggested the EU should be ready to ask a court to block access to platforms temporarily if necessary "once other powers have been exhausted and where an infringement persists and causes serious harm."
The lawmakers said the measure was "not about censoring a service or banning a social network; it is about no longer brandishing a threat that nobody believes in."
Fines could be "written off" by tech titans, they argued, but a "shutdown ordered by a judge reaches the business model itself."
The lawmakers accused von der Leyen of failing to deliver on a political pledge to make online spaces safer for children.
"Will the protection of minors online still be among your priorities?" they wrote. "The commission speaks but does not deliver."
The EU began its probe into Meta in 2024 under the Digital Services Act (DSA), a content law that has been fiercely criticised by the United States.
The law is a major weapon in the EU's boosted legal arsenal agreed in recent years to rein in Big Tech firms.
The EU is due to announce some form of ban on social media for children later this month – although the full details are not yet known.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Government acknowledges need to strengthen airport security to curb drug smuggling
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: The government acknowledges that there are still areas that need to be improved in the country's outbound and inbound security systems, particularly at airports, to curb drug smuggling.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government was taking steps to strengthen security measures involving various agencies following several cases of Malaysians being arrested for drug-related offences after arriving in other countries.
"We acknowledge that there are still a few areas that need to be improved in our outbound and inbound systems, particularly at the country's entry points, including airports, to curb drug smuggling.
"This involves all agencies, including the police, Immigration Department, the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency under the Home Ministry, as well as aviation security, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and others," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after handing over the RM80.1 million Third Region Marine Police Base project in Tok Bali here today.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry had jointly prepared a proposal to strengthen security measures at entry points, particularly airports.
"The plan has 17 measures and will be implemented in three phases: short, medium and long term.
"It involves both outbound and inbound security because we have identified several cases involving Malaysians who left the country and were subsequently arrested in their destination countries," he said.
Saifuddin said such cases needed to be addressed carefully while respecting the laws and sovereignty of the countries where Malaysians were arrested.
"I have been asked whether Malaysia will bring back our citizens caught overseas, like in the case of the pilot who was arrested in Indonesia.
"I told them that if our citizens are arrested there, the country where they arrive is the one that will enforce its laws.
"That country is sovereign and independent, and it has the right to enforce its laws," he said.
Saifuddin said Malaysian authorities could, however, seek access to Malaysians detained overseas to interview them and assist in investigations.
He said close police-to-police relations and Asean cooperation had enabled Malaysian authorities to work with their counterparts in neighbouring countries.
"Through the investigation involving the pilot, for example, we obtained a lot of
information.
"Based on that information, we made further arrests," he said.
He said the cooperation was important to determine whether those arrested had acted alone or were part of an established criminal syndicate.
"We need to establish whether the individual acted alone or whether there is an established criminal syndicate behind the activity.
"We will look into all these aspects," he said.
Saifuddin also credited the police, particularly the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, for acting swiftly and maintaining close cooperation with law enforcement agencies in neighbouring countries.
He was commenting on the latest case involving a 62-year-old Malaysian man who was arrested by Indian Customs authorities at Chennai International Airport after he was allegedly caught smuggling 3.452kg of hydroponic cannabis worth about 1.20 crore rupees (RM520,000) into the country on Aug 31.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farm Fresh to raise RM200mil to fuel Cambodian expansion, Inside Scoop buyout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Farm Fresh Bhd is seeking to raise up to RM200 million through a proposed private placement to aggressively scale its regional dairy footprint and consolidate its stake in premium ice cream maker The Inside Scoop.
The integrated dairy group announced that it intends to issue up to 109.65 million new ordinary shares, representing roughly 5.8 per cent of its existing share capital, based on the illustrative issue price of RM1.8240.
A major portion of the proceeds, amounting to RM148.3 million, has been earmarked for capital expenditure over the next 24 months. Of this, a substantial RM92 million will be directed toward accelerating the group's ambitions in Cambodia.
Farm Fresh plans to enhance its local processing facilities with new ultra-high temperature (UHT) production lines and develop a large-scale integrated dairy farm in the Pursat province alongside local partners.
This strategic move is expected to lower regional logistics costs and capture growing structural demand in the broader Indochina market.
"The proposed investments are expected to strengthen the group's production footprint regionally, improve production economics through lower logistics costs, support future demand growth and provide a platform for further expansion within Cambodia and the broader Indochina market," the group said.
Domestically, Farm Fresh will channel RM56.3 million toward expanding its Larkin processing facility and venturing into new, complementary fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) segments to broaden its product portfolio.
Beyond infrastructure, RM50.0 million of the placement proceeds will be used to settle a put option exercised by Edmund Tan, co-founder of The Inside Scoop Sdn Bhd (TISSB).
Farm Fresh received a notice on Aug 28 requiring the group to acquire an additional 20 per cent equity interest in Inside Scoop from Tan, further deepening Farm Fresh's ownership of the popular dessert chain.
The board noted that the equity fund-raising exercise is the most appropriate avenue to quickly secure capital while improving the group's debt headroom.
Following the placement, Farm Fresh's pro forma gearing is expected to improve from 0.89 times to 0.53 times. The proposal is slated for completion by the third quarter of 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Serian records hazardous API reading at 400
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Serian in Sarawak recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 400 as of 6pm today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy readings, with Sri Aman recording 273, followed by Samarahan (272) and Sarikei (202).
Another 10 areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan recorded unhealthy API readings.
Six locations in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings. This includes Mukah (172), Bintulu (165), Kapit (155), ILP Miri (153), Limbang (151) and Miri (102).
In Sabah, Kota Kinabalu (156), Kimanis (154) and Keningau (153) recorded unhealthy readings.
Labuan recorded an unhealthy reading of 156.
Meanwhile, 37 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings, while four areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are considered hazardous.

Title: TH investment arm to come under SC regulation
Article:
BANGI: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) plans to place its investment arm under the supervision of the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) as part of changes to its regulatory framework.
TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain said the proposal to place the investment arm under a statutory regulator, particularly the SC, was reached following extensive discussions by a joint task force.
The task force involved SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour.
"After considering the matter in detail for almost six months, we concluded that it would be more appropriate for TH's investment arm to be regulated by the SC. However, this does not mean BNM will no longer be involved.
"We are refining the framework to ensure all key regulators are involved in TH's regulatory structure in the future," he said while speaking as a panellist at the 'Dialog Ummah: Realiti dan Masa Depan Tabung Haji' organised by Himpunan Gerakan Islam Malaysia here today.
Rashid said the main reason the SC was chosen as the primary regulator was because between 90 and 95 per cent of TH's total assets were invested in the capital market rather than held in pure liquidity.
Therefore, he said, the SC's regulatory jurisdiction was aligned with TH's core portfolio structure, as most of the institution's operations were directly linked to capital market investments.
"BNM will continue to have a role in overseeing the financial institution as a whole and the stability of the country's financial system. Matters relating to liquidity will always remain under BNM's jurisdiction," he said.
Rashid said liquidity played an important role as a secondary buffer to mitigate potential crises or liquidity shortages in the event of a sudden loss of depositor confidence.
On the legislative changes required to establish the new regulatory framework, he said proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act would be submitted soon.
However, he said the process would take time as it required the involvement of stakeholders.
He said detailed technical provisions were needed to ensure TH remained fully intact as an Islamic financial and savings institution.
He said its investment arm would continue to be strengthened through regulatory oversight to ensure higher safety standards for depositors.
"The process of amending an Act involves several formal stages. The proposal must first be submitted to the minister, who will then bring it to the cabinet for approval.
"Once approved by the cabinet, it will go through the Attorney-General's Chambers for final drafting before being tabled," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH RCI findings mirror FGV case, says PMO adviser
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Issues involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) bear similarities to the case involving FGV Holdings Bhd, based on findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrimage fund, says Prime Minister's Office economic adviser Nurhisham Hussein.
He said reading the RCI report reminded him of similar findings involving government-linked organisations in the past.
He said the TH case was similar to FGV as both involved investment issues.
"The issue is the same. Assets for the pilgrimage fund were acquired without adequate guarantees, at inflated prices and without proper due diligence.
"All this appears to show a similar pattern to what happened at FGV Holdings," he said during the Dialog Ummah: Realiti dan Masa Depan TH programme here today.
FGV Holdings is a subsidiary of Felda, which the government has had to allocate almost RM1 billion annually to meet its financial commitments and debts.
In July, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported to have said that Felda faced losses of almost RM10 billion due to mismanagement and excessive political interference.
Some depositors have raised concerns over whether the government can shoulder the burden following the RCI's findings of financial mismanagement at TH.
Nurhisham said Malaysia was "not Argentina or Greece", referring to the debt crises faced by the two countries that pushed them towards bankruptcy.
"The Malaysian government has never failed to meet its financial obligations. We have always made the payments," he said.
Meanwhile, Nurhisham said that the issuance of RM11.5 billion in sukuk was not a bailout of TH, but a refinancing exercise that would provide the institution with a more sustainable cash flow.
He said the new sukuk replaced earlier sukuk issued by Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB).
"The original sukuk issued by UJSB was zero-coupon, meaning TH did not receive annual returns from it.
"When the earlier sukuk matured, it was replaced with new sukuk that provided annual returns. This benefits TH as the institution receives cash flow every year," he added.
On the risk profile of the issuance, Nurhisham said the potential financial risk of the sukuk was ultimately borne by the government, rather than TH or its depositors.
He said the value of the sukuk largely depended on the value of existing assets managed by UJSB.
"If UJSB is unable to realise the full value of those assets, the government will still fulfil its obligations under the Tabung Haji Act to protect all depositors' funds," he said.
The RCI report concluded that a combination of excessive hibah commitments, questionable accounting practices, weak oversight, overly ambitious investment strategies and increased subsidy responsibilities placed significant financial pressure on TH between 2014 and 2020.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia will not protect, harbour southern Thai militants
Article:
PASIR PUTEH: Malaysia will never protect or harbour anyone involved in misconduct or acts of violence in southern Thailand, including militants alleged to be hiding in the country.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government had no intention of protecting anyone found to be involved in wrongdoing or violent activities.
He said Malaysia and Thailand had several established mechanisms to address security and border-related issues, including government-to-government (G2G) engagements through joint authorities and the Border Working Group, which meets regularly to discuss matters concerning the common border.
"At the police level, there is also a police-to-police (P2P) mechanism involving security discussions between both countries.
"If Thailand conveys any matter of concern to them, we will listen and address it. Likewise, we will raise matters that concern us with them," he said after handing over the RM80 million Third Region Marine Police Base project here today.
Saifuddin said people-to-people ties were also important given the close interaction between the neighbouring countries.
"Malaysia has never protected anyone involved in misconduct or incidents of violence in southern Thailand, including militants alleged to be hiding in this country.
"We will use the existing mechanisms to manage the issue as it involves relations between two countries," he said.
He urged all parties not to fuel tensions or create suspicion over allegations involving militants and cross-border security issues, saying security agencies on both sides should be allowed to conduct their respective investigations.
"I think, at this stage, we should not add fuel to the situation or create an atmosphere of suspicion.
"The best way to handle this issue is through our security forces. The police will conduct their investigations, while the authorities on the other side will conduct theirs.
"We will use the existing mechanisms to manage the issue because relations between two countries cannot be managed based solely on sentiment and emotions.
"We have a great responsibility towards the people," he said.
Asked whether there were cases of militants across the border, Saifuddin declined to give a definitive answer.
"I do not want to say yes or no because whether militants are on this side, or whether individuals on our wanted list are on their side, are matters that have been discussed for decades.
"What I want to stress is that the matter is being handled through the existing mechanisms, and we will make the best use of them.
"I will not touch on that particular matter. I have full confidence in the process," he said.
Saifuddin also urged the media to be mindful of sensitivities when reporting issues involving the security and bilateral relations of the two countries.
Also present at the event were Federal Internal Security and Public Order director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China artists quit South Korea exhibition over Taiwan row
Article:
SEOUL: Chinese artists withdrew from a major South Korean art show after organisers allowed "Taiwan" to be used in the name of an exhibition, officials said Thursday, as China issued a rebuke.
The Gwangju Biennale, one of Asia's largest contemporary art events, is due to open Saturday, with its Pavilion Project bringing together artists from around the world at venues across the southwestern city.
The dispute began after Taiwanese artists said organisers had initially agreed to call their exhibition the "Taiwan Pavilion", but changed the name in June to "NTMoFA", the acronym for Taiwan's National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts.
The change was made "without the consent of the participating team, and brutally erased Taiwan from the poster," the artists said in a joint statement last month, accusing organisers of "political censorship."
China insists Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex the self-ruled island of more than 23 million people.
Last week, the Gwangju Biennale foundation reversed course and agreed to restore the name "Taiwan Pavilion."
Chinese artists then halted preparations for their own pavilion, and on Thursday, the Chinese artists announced they would formally withdraw, according to local media footage.
A spokesperson for the foundation told AFP: "We have confirmation the Chinese artists are withdrawing from the biennale."
China's consulate general in Gwangju said Biennale organisers "openly allowed the Taiwan region of China to participate in the exhibition using a name that is completely inconsistent with its status."
"This constitutes a serious violation of the One China principle," it said, adding: "We once again urge the organisers of the Gwangju Biennale to immediately rectify their wrongdoing."
South Korea's foreign ministry spoke up to calm the row, saying that the "government's basic position regarding Taiwan remains unchanged."
The ministry said the decision was made in the cultural and artistic sphere, and "is unrelated to the South Korean government's position regarding Taiwan."
"We hope that this issue will not affect South Korea-China relations or exchanges and cooperation between the two countries," they added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No political appointments, interference at TH, says chairman
Article:
BANGI: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has made no political appointments or faced political interference under its current leadership as the institution moves towards a more professional governance structure, says its chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain.
He said he had not allowed any politician to be appointed to TH's board since taking over as chairman in 2023, adding that the institution must be managed professionally as a credible Islamic financial institution.
"Since I entered TH, I basically haven't allowed a single politician to be appointed to TH.
"I'm very lucky. I worked with two very good ministers, my previous minister and this minister, who understood that I'm not a politician and I do not want politics in TH," he told reporters after the Dialog Ummah: Realiti dan Masa Depan TH programme here today.
Rashid said TH should be treated as a credible Islamic financial institution and managed professionally to facilitate the haj pilgrimage and serve the Muslim community.
He said the current board's composition was based on two key principles recommended by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI): fit and proper criteria, and a balance of skills required by the institution.
He said the approach had enabled the board to take a more hands-on role through various board committees, while ensuring decisions were based on professional expertise.
"And Alhamdulillah, there has not been any political interference whatsoever. I can assure you that from both ministers I have worked with," he said.
Rashid said the professional management approach had contributed to TH's financial recovery, including strengthening its balance sheet, building reserves and returning the institution to profitability.
He said TH had recorded higher profits and dividends over the past three years, with the positive trend expected to continue.
"We are very much on the road to recovery, and we have done so. We have cleaned up the balance sheet, started building reserves, written off everything, and put proper governance measures in place," he said.
Asked about the most challenging RCI recommendations to resolve, Rashid said TH had implemented 76 per cent of the 25 recommendations.
"In fact, it involves external parties. The external links are not that easy because it's a long process," he said.
On July 29, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) published the 211-page RCI report on the investigation into TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
The report outlined various weaknesses in the institution's management during the period and made 25 recommendations for improvement. As of July 30, TH had implemented 75 per cent of them.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Haji considers placing investment arm under SC oversight
Article:
BANGI: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) is evaluating a proposed shift in its regulatory framework to place its investment operations under formal statutory oversight.
TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain said a joint task force committee, which includes the Securities Commission (SC) chairman and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) governor, has leaned toward placing TH's investment arm under SC oversight following extensive internal deliberations.
"After deliberating in detail for almost six months, we concluded that it is more relevant for Tabung Haji to be regulated by the SC.
"However, that does not mean BNM will not be involved.
"We are fine-tuning the framework to ensure all key regulators are involved in TH's future regulatory structure," Abdul Rashid said during a panel session titled "Dialog Ummah: Realiti dan Masa Depan Tabung Haji" organised by Himpunan Gerakan Islam Malaysia here today.
He said the primary reason for choosing the SC as the main regulator is that 90 to 95 per cent of TH's total assets are invested in capital markets rather than held in pure liquidity.
Because the majority of TH's operations pertain directly to capital market investments, he said the SC's regulatory jurisdiction aligns naturally with the core structure of TH's portfolio.
While the SC is being eyed as the primary regulator for its investment operations, BNM will retain an essential role in overseeing overall financial stability, Abdul Rashid said.
"BNM will maintain overarching responsibility over the country's financial institutions and total financial system stability.
"Liquidity matters will always remain under BNM's purview," he said.
He added that liquidity plays a critical role as a secondary fallback to mitigate potential liquidity crises or runs in the event of a sudden loss of depositor confidence, referencing BNM's historical role as an informal monitor between 2014 and 2017.
Addressing the legislative changes required to enact the new regulatory framework, Abdul Rashid said proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act will be submitted soon, noting that the process will take time due to necessary stakeholder engagements.
The technical details must ensure that TH remains completely intact as a religious and savings institution, he said, while its investment arm will be clearly identified and carved out for formal regulatory oversight to guarantee a higher standard of safety for depositors.
"The process of amending an act involves several formal stages.
"The proposal must first be presented to the minister, who will then take it to the Cabinet for approval. Once agreed, it will go through the Attorney-General's Chambers for final drafting before being tabled," Abdul Rashid added. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil servants demerit system not a punitive tool, says Chief Secretary
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Demerit Performance Evaluation (DEEP) implemented for senior public service management is not intended as a punitive measure against officers who fail to meet the prescribed performance standards.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the system was one of the mechanisms under the public service reform agenda aimed at improving leadership quality among senior management.
"We have analysed the DEEP performance results for the second quarter of 2026.
"As I mentioned previously, DEEP is not intended to punish, but to improve the leadership of public servants, particularly those in the senior management of the public service," he said.
He said this when met after attending the closing ceremony of the 2026 Public Sector AI Seminar and the presentation of the Public Sector AI Nexus Challenge 2026 awards here today.
Asked whether officers who fail to achieve the prescribed merit threshold could face action such as demotion, Shamsul Azri reiterated that DEEP was not established as a punitive measure.
"As I said earlier, it is not to punish, but to improve," he said.
Yesterday, it was reported that the Public Service Department (PSD) had been asked to review the assessment weightings under DEEP for ministry secretary-general positions.
Shamsul Azri said the move was aimed at ensuring the performance assessment system for senior public service management remained holistic and relevant, while reflecting the evolving challenges of public administration.
"Moving forward, I have asked PSD to review the DEEP weightings for secretary-generals so that they do not focus solely on development projects, but also take into account a combination of high-impact and people-centric projects.
"Digitalisation should also be part of the performance indicators, including the extent to which ministries are able to transition to paperless operations. We want performance measurements that truly reflect the changes led and the outcomes experienced by the people," he said.
He said performance assessments of top public service leadership must focus on actual outcomes and impact.

Title: Spanish PM says no 'solid proof' Morocco planned Ceuta migrant rush
Article:
MADRID: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Thursday insisted there was no "solid proof" Morocco orchestrated July's migrant rush into Ceuta, after a police report highlighted multiple failings by Moroccan security forces.
But the Socialist leader slammed "unacceptable" Moroccan government comments about Ceuta since the crisis began, in rare public criticism of neighbouring Rabat which claims the north African enclave.
Sanchez also risked inflaming delicate relations with Morocco by revealing the government had urged King Felipe VI to visit Ceuta and Spain's other north African territory of Melilla.
More than 70,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta from Morocco on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented surge that left scores dead, most by drowning as they tried to swim around a breakwater.
The leftist government has consistently avoided blaming Morocco, with which it has spent years trying to improve historically complicated relations – notably over the status of Ceuta and Melilla.
But a Spanish police report seen by AFP on Wednesday flagged a Moroccan police response of "total permissiveness" that facilitated the rush, with some officers directing migrants towards the water.
Police numbers around the border post were "clearly smaller than usual" and officers "made no serious attempt" to stem the surge, said the report, based on satellite images, open-source videos and migrant testimonies.
Addressing parliament on Thursday to offer explanations about the crisis, Sanchez said no police, legal or international institutions had submitted "solid proof to the government of Spain that Morocco planned or executed the incident."
"If this solid proof existed, we would act accordingly," said Sanchez, who added that "this government is not afraid of confronting other foreign powers."
Sanchez also slammed "unacceptable" comments about Ceuta and Melilla by two Moroccan government ministers, revealing Spain summoned Morocco's ambassador on Aug 21.
[[nid:1525056]]
Moroccan media quoted Justice Minister Abdellatif Ouahbi in August as saying Rabat had "historic" and "geographical" rights over Ceuta and Melilla, calling for a "final solution" that would allow the territories to "return to the fold of the motherland."
Ceuta and Melilla – which share the European Union's only land borders with Africa – will remain Spanish "until the end of time", Sanchez told parliament on Thursday.
Although most of the migrants who streamed into Ceuta have since returned to Morocco, thousands continue to roam the small city's streets and sleep rough, increasing tensions among locals who feel abandoned.
Tens of thousands of people protested in Ceuta and across Spain on Wednesday over the leftist government's handling of the crisis, with the conservative and far-right opposition using the rallies to attack Sanchez.
The opposition has consistently cast doubt on Morocco's role and accuse Sanchez of being subservient to Rabat.
Some analysts have suggested Morocco used the migrant rush to exert political pressure on Spain after Sanchez visited Rabat's historic enemy Algeria in July.
The disputed Western Sahara is a source of tension, with Morocco largely controlling the former Spanish colony that is claimed by the Algerian-backed pro-independence Polisario Front.
Yet Spain reversed its long-standing policy of neutrality in 2022, backing Rabat's autonomy plan for the territory under Moroccan sovereignty – infuriating Algeria.
Sanchez also revealed the government had urged King Felipe to travel Ceuta and Melilla "in the coming weeks", in rare public comments about royal matters.
Such a visit would likely spark tensions with Morocco, after the last trip by a Spanish monarch to the cities in 2007 sparked a diplomatic crisis.
"Ceuta needs to be supported by the state more than ever," Sanchez said in justification of the plea.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ministries must spend according to respective budget - Chief Secretary
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar stressed that ministries and government agencies must spend according to their allocated budgets.
However, he declined to comment further on the open dispute between the finance ministry (MoF) and the rural and regional development ministry (KKDW).
"That should be asked of Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.
"But in the public service, spending must be in accordance with what has been budgeted," he said when met after attending the closing ceremony of the 2026 Public Sector AI Seminar and the presentation of the Public Sector AI Nexus Challenge 2026 awards today.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi raised the issue of delayed payments to contractors carrying out development projects last Tuesday.
He said some contractors had completed projects and achieved the required progress, but faced delays in receiving payments.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the
delays occurred
because allocations that were supposed to be channelled to his ministry had yet to be received.
However, Johan then said
KKDW had, for several years
, made commitments and spent beyond its approved annual allocations for rural road projects.
He said in 2023, KKDW's actual expenditure amounted to RM1.8 billion, compared with an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion.
In 2024, actual expenditure stood at RM2 billion against an approved allocation of RM1.3 billion, while in 2025, actual expenditure reached RM2.3 billion compared with an approved allocation of RM1.6 billion.
For this year, Johan said the approved allocation for KKDW amounted to RM2.1 billion, while actual expenditure had reached RM1.9 billion as of June.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King grants audience to Singapore Foreign Minister

According to Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's Facebook post, the audience took place at Pavilion 2 of Istana Pasir Pelangi Polo Grounds, here.
