Title: Malaysian man critically injured in Yogyakarta crash, family seeks RM50,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 30-year-old Malaysian man is in critical condition in Indonesia after the car he was driving collided with a lorry at Km99 of the Cipali Toll Road on Sunday.
The victim, Ahmad Tarmizi Hazmee, suffered severe injuries, including a fractured jaw, shattered cheekbone, broken right arm, fractured ribs, as well as brain swelling and bleeding.
The accident, which occurred while they were travelling from Yogyakarta to Jakarta to return home, also claimed the life of his youngest brother, Muhammad Atiqullah, 20, at the scene.
Three other passengers, Ahmad Tarmizi's wife, child, and another brother, Adam, 25, sustained minor injuries.
Atiqullah's remains were buried at the Dunguswiru Public Cemetery in Subang Kota on Aug 30 with the assistance of the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta and local police.
The victim's eldest brother, Ahmad Bukhari, 32, said Ahmad Tarmizi is currently semi-conscious at the Mitra Plumbon Subang Hospital in West Java and requires an estimated RM50,000 to cover medical and surgical costs.
"Tarmizi successfully underwent his first surgery on Aug 31. However, his condition remains unstable, and he shows aggressive movement whenever sedation is stopped, requiring doctors to re-administer it so he can rest.
"He is still reliant on a ventilator, and there are plans to transfer him to a hospital in Jakarta for further treatment due to inadequate facilities at the current hospital," he said when contacted.
Ahmad Bukhari said hospital treatment costs have already reached RM30,000, and although public donations have helped raise about RM30,000, the amount is expected to rise depending on the hospital transfer and future medical evacuation flight costs to Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Serian records hazardous API 391, four other Sarawak areas at very unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, September 3 — Air quality continued to deteriorate this afternoon, with Serian in Sarawak recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 391, putting it in the hazardous category, while four other areas in the state recorded very unhealthy readings.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said four areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Kuching registering an API reading of 285, Sri Aman 275, Samarahan 274 and Sarikei 206.
As of 5pm, 14 areas were classified as having unhealthy air quality, while 45 were at moderate levels and three were in the good category, she said.
Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality, with Sibu registering an API reading of 180, followed by Mukah (172), Bintulu (166), Samalaju (164), Kapit (157), ILP Miri (153), Limbang (151) and Miri (106).
Other areas recording unhealthy air quality included Politeknik Kota Kinabalu and Kota Kinabalu in Sabah, both at 156, Kimanis (155), Keningau (154), Labuan Federal Territory (157) and Johan Setia in Selangor (127).
“The country’s air quality has deteriorated today, with several areas, especially in Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan, recording API readings ranging from unhealthy to hazardous, influenced by haze moving in from different directions,” she said.
She said that according to an Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated September 2, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) 20 satellite imagery detected 795 hotspots in Kalimantan, 144 in Sumatra and three in Malaysia, all in Sarawak.
She said the ASMC Regional Haze Map for the same date showed scattered hotspots across Kalimantan and Sumatra, while moderate to dense transboundary smoke haze covered northern Borneo and parts of the southwestern, western and central Philippines.
“Moderate to dense smoke was also observed originating from clusters of hotspots detected in several areas of Kalimantan and central and southern Sumatra.
“The Asean Secretariat activated Alert Level 3 for the southern Asean region from August 27, 2026 following an increase in hotspot activity and the wider spread of haze, based on ASMC monitoring, assessments and forecasts and in accordance with the Asean MAJER SOP (Asean Standard Operating Procedure for Monitoring Assessment and Joint Emergency Response),” she said.
She said the DOE would continue to monitor air quality through the National Haze Action Plan, with the relevant agencies taking action based on the situation and its developments. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia probes claim subsidised padi fertiliser smuggled into Thailand for bomb-making
Article:
PASIR PUTEH, September 3 — Malaysia and Thailand will use existing bilateral mechanisms to investigate allegations of bomb-making activities involving fertiliser elements from Malaysia, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the Malaysian and Thai police would conduct their respective investigations, with the matter to be managed through established channels, including government-to-government engagement, the Border Working Group and Police-to-Police (P-to-P) cooperation.
“The police will conduct an investigation, the authorities on their side will also conduct an investigation, and we will use the mechanisms that I mentioned,” he told a media conference after the handover ceremony for the completed Marine Police Base, Region Three project in Tok Bali here today.
He said that he would not want to respond directly to every allegation that emerged, stressing that border-related issues should instead be addressed through the mechanisms already established between the two countries.
According to him, the approach was important to prevent tensions from escalating or mutual suspicion from arising between the two sides, as Malaysia and Thailand had major responsibilities towards their respective peoples.
Saifuddin Nasution said the P-to-P cooperation enabled enforcement authorities from both countries to communicate and discuss security-related matters at any time, describing the mechanism as operating continuously.
Meanwhile, the Border Working Group serves as another platform for Malaysia and Thailand to discuss matters concerning the border, he said.
On the Region Three Marine Police Base, he said it is expected to begin operations in November with 111 officers and personnel to strengthen enforcement and maritime security along the East Coast.
The RM80.01 million project, implemented by PBLT Sdn Bhd, includes an administration building, boathouse, mechanical workshop, jetty, guardhouse, ammunition store and 82 quarters for personnel.
Saifuddin Nasution said the base would strengthen efforts to counter threats in East Coast waters, including drug and firearm smuggling, illegal immigrant and refugee landings, as well as incursions by fishermen.
“Most importantly, we are safeguarding the sovereignty of the country’s waters,” he said.
Also present were Bukit Aman Department of Internal Security and Public Order director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. — Bernama

Title: Contractor: Muhyiddin’s Bersatu donation request wasn’t my imagination, I didn’t report it fearing abetment accusations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff today insisted that former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin told him in July 2020 that Bumiputera contractors who received Jana Wibawa projects could donate directly to the latter’s party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
Azman, who was testifying as the 27th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, confirmed his previous testimony that he viewed Muhyiddin’s donation request as an offence.
Quizzed by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, Azman confirmed that he had never lodged a police report against Muhyiddin over the donation request and disagreed that he had imagined the request.
Amer:
I’m telling you the reason why you didn’t make the complaint is because the so-called request is nothing more than a figment of your imagination.
Azman:
Disagree.
Later, when asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin, Azman initially insisted that Muhyiddin had made the request, adding that he did not lodge a report as he “akur” or complied with Muhyiddin’s request.
But after a short break, Azman told the High Court judge that he wanted to correct his answer as he had remembered why he did not lodge a police report against Muhyiddin.
“I did not lodge a report because I don’t want to be accused of ‘bersubahat’ (abetting) Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin,” he said.
Among other things, Azman earlier today confirmed that Muhyiddin did not contact him in 2021 or 2022 to ask about any donations from contractors to Bersatu.
Amer then suggested that this meant the July 2020 discussion between Azman and Muhyiddin was merely a “creation” by the contractor so that he could “point the finger” at the former prime minister.
But Azman disagreed.
Earlier, Azman had said that Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) committee member and Bersatu leader Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was closer to Muhyiddin than he was.
But Azman disagreed with Amer’s suggestion that this meant Muhyiddin would not have asked him to tell other contractors to donate to Bersatu, and also disagreed that Muhyiddin would have asked someone close to him instead.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex. — File picture by Firdaus Latif
Azman denies making deal with MACC in own corruption case, insists he’s innocent
Separately, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had previously investigated Azman in 2023 over allegations that he had asked for and received bribes from contractors as a reward for helping them obtain Jana Wibawa projects.
Azman confirmed that the complaint that prompted MACC’s investigation mentioned his name but not Muhyiddin’s.
Azman confirmed to Amer that he had faced financial constraints when his accounts were frozen for nine months and agreed that the operations of his company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and related company Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd were disrupted during that period.
Azman agreed that he was under economic pressure in 2023 because of these events, but disagreed with Amer that this had caused him to “play ball” with MACC or that the commission had him “in their grip”.
Amer went on to suggest that Azman’s court testimony against Muhyiddin had been modified to fit MACC’s narrative and that he had tailored his testimony because he was under economic duress and pressure in 2023.
Azman disagreed.
Azman also disagreed with Amer’s suggestion that he had made a deal with MACC to testify against Muhyiddin and avoid being prosecuted, as his company KCJ Engineering would stand to lose its RM62 million Jana Wibawa contract if he were found guilty in court.
Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin (pictured) questioned Azman Yusoff over why he did not lodge a police report against Muhyiddin. — File picture by Firdaus Latif
Later, when asked about the complaint that led to MACC’s 2023 investigation against him, Azman told the prosecution that the complaint was a “defamation” against him.
“That is a ‘fitnah’ (defamation) against me. I come to court to speak the truth, and I don’t care whether Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin wins or loses in this case. What is important, I am in court to speak the truth and I have already taken the oath,” he told Wan Shaharuddin.
Azman confirmed that he had not been remanded or charged in his own corruption case, but insisted that he had not committed any wrongdoing and claimed he was innocent.
Azman argued that bribery cases involved those with power, such as the prime minister, while saying that he himself did not have the power to award projects and that he had told contractors to donate to Bersatu if they obtained the projects.
Later, when explaining why he did not think the millions of ringgit received by his associated companies were bribes, Azman said he did not have the power to award projects, appoint contractors or receive donations, and also insisted that those in power would use their positions to ask for bribes.
Azman previously confirmed that his associated companies KCJ Engineering and Addeen Engineering received a total of RM9.35 million from several contractors, including RM1 million from Nepturis Sdn Bhd and RM600,000 from Mamfor Sdn Bhd.
Earlier, Azman insisted to Amer that the money he had received from those contractors was from “business deals” between companies and claimed that the payments were for technical advice he had provided on material costs for projects.
When clarifying why he had previously denied “selling” Muhyiddin’s name to obtain money from Bumiputera contractors Nepturis and Mamfor, Azman told the prosecution that he was “tidaklah sejahat” (not as evil) as to sell Muhyiddin’s name and added that he was indebted to the latter for his actions during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Azman concluded his testimony after confirming to the judge that he remains an Umno member.
Yesterday, MACC investigator Mazery Mohd Zaini said three Bumiputera contractors and their representatives had given RM25.3 million to Bersatu after obtaining Jana Wibawa projects, namely Azman and KCJ Engineering, which gave RM4.8 million; Nepturis, which gave RM1 million; and Mamfor, which gave RM19.5 million after its associated company Sutracom Sdn Bhd obtained a project.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, comprising four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd, and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume on September 14.

Title: MetMalaysia conducts cloud seeding over Perlis, Kedah to boost dam water levels
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, September 3 — The government has carried out a cloud seeding operation (OPA) in Perlis and Kedah today as an early, targeted measure to address dry weather, low rainfall and deteriorating air quality risks.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said in a statement that the operation focused on increasing rainfall over targeted areas and catchments to help boost and maintain water levels at major dams.
It said the initiative was crucial to ensure an uninterrupted water supply for domestic and agricultural use during the dry spell.
Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) secretary-general Datuk Anis Rizana Mohd Zainudin joined the flight to observe the operational process, technical requirements and challenges faced by the team.
The target locations included the Timah Tasoh Dam in Perlis, as well as the Ahning, Pedu, Muda and Beris dams in Kedah.
A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) C-130H aircraft from No. 20 Squadron, Subang Air Base, was used for the operation, carrying four tanks of salt solution for cloud seeding.
Prepared as early as 8am, each tank contained a mixture of about 200 kilogrammes of sodium chloride (NaCl) and 1,500 litres of water before the aircraft took off at 12.30pm.
The mission was led by RMAF Mission Commander Maj Mohammad Syaaban Zainal Abidin, alongside pilot Maj Mohamad Saifullah Mohamad and co-pilots Capt Mohd Fuad Mohd Nazir and Lt Muhammad Awais Fahmi Abdul Razak.
Also on board were navigator Lt Muhammad Zulhafizie Mat Zam, flight engineer Maj Muhammad Khairi Khamis, and loadmasters Air Warrant Officer II Zamzuri Mat Jusoh, Air Sergeant Muhd Nur Ezzat Ismail and Air Sergeant Muhammad Syazwan Mohd Yusoff.
Cloud seeding was first carried out over the Timah Tasoh Dam before the aircraft headed to the Ahning Dam, where seeding was skipped due to a lack of suitable cloud formation.
The aircraft then proceeded to other dams in Kedah, spraying the salt solution where cloud conditions met the technical criteria before completing the operation at 3.30pm.
MetMalaysia said the success of the operation depended on suitable cloud formations and atmospheric conditions, with each flight guided by scientific assessments and meteorological analysis.
Observations showed the operation was conducted at altitudes between 5,000 and 9,000 feet, depending on cloud formations.
MetMalaysia noted that cloud seeding operations conducted across several states this year - including Perlis, Kedah, Perak, Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah - achieved a 90 per cent success rate in generating rainfall over target or catchment areas.
The operation was a strategic collaboration involving the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), MetMalaysia and the RMAF, with Nadma coordinating funding, the RMAF providing flight support, and MetMalaysia supplying technical expertise.
MetMalaysia added that the government would continue to consider further cloud seeding operations as a mitigation measure against the El Nino phenomenon and haze episodes, subject to atmospheric conditions and cloud suitability. — Bernama

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher, FBM KLCI gains 6.39 points as BNM holds OPR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, tracking positive cues from Wall Street, with sentiment further bolstered by Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent.
At 5 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 6.39 points 1,715.13, compared with yesterday’s close of 1,708.74.
The benchmark index opened 2.42 points higher at 1,711.16 and fluctuated between 1,708.47 and 1,716.23 throughout the day.
The broader market was also positive with gainers outnumbering losers 625 to 497, while 591 counters were unchanged, 1,059 untraded and 17 suspended.
Turnover declined to 3.90 billion units valued at RM3.21 billion from 4.20 billion units valued at RM3.52 billion on Wednesday.
In a statement today, BNM said the latest indicators point to resilient global growth, supported by strong global tech expansion, improving supply conditions and stable labour markets.
It said inflation has edged lower in recent months but is expected to remain elevated given the lagged pass-through of energy costs to consumer prices.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said the FBM KLCI closed higher, tracking broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight, as optimism over the interest-rate outlook outweighed concerns about persistent global inflationary pressures.
“Sentiment was further supported by weaker-than-expected US private-sector job growth, which strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve may have greater scope to ease monetary policy,” he said.
Mohd Sedek said the market gained further momentum after the lunch break following BNM’s decision to maintain the OPR at 2.75 per cent, in line with expectations. The decision provided greater clarity on the domestic monetary policy outlook and lifted buying interest in index-linked counters.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank eased two sen to RM10.58, Public Bank added seven sen to RM5.00, CIMB Group gained 15 sen to RM7.99, Tenaga Nasional rose four sen to RM13.68, while IHH Healthcare slipped nine sen to RM7.99.

Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index surged 128.06 points to 20,206.83, the Energy Index gained 8.08 points to 810.03, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.38 of a point to 187.16, while the Plantation Index shrank 33.45 points to 9,494.02.
