Title: ‘You were supposed to come back today’: Wife marks anniversary as firefighter husband remains missing in Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A 10th wedding anniversary, an occasion that should have been marked with gifts and quality time together, has instead become a period of anxious waiting for Hani Othman, whose husband, Senior Fire Officer II (PBK II) Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, remains missing following a flood tragedy in Rasuwa, Nepal, on August 26.
On their anniversary today, Hani took to Facebook to express her hope that her husband, affectionately known as Loe, would return home as promised.
“You were supposed to come back today. You promised to bring home an anniversary gift. I’m nervous wondering what gift you’re going to give me this year,” she wrote.
For Hani, Loe’s return would mean more than celebrating their anniversary. It would also allow the couple to pursue the many dreams they had planned together.
Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who remains missing following floods in Nepal, is pictured with his wife, Hani Othman. — Picture via Facebook/Hani Othman
They are scheduled to sit for the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) examination under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) framework on September 6. In October, they planned to attend a diving course on Tioman Island to obtain their divemaster certifications.
The couple had also planned to climb Mount Rinjani in May and Mount Kilimanjaro in August next year. Loe’s greatest ambition was to reach the summit of Mount Everest, an achievement he hoped to accomplish alongside Hani.
“I told you we would train together and that I would accompany you all the way to the summit of Everest this time, didn’t I? Your dream of reaching the Everest summit hasn’t been fulfilled yet. Please, where are you?” Hani wrote.
Mohd Fakhrul Munir, 44, a member of the Fire and Rescue Department’s Air Special Operations Unit (PASKUB), was reported missing after the expedition team he was travelling with was caught in flooding, believed to have occurred in a valley in Rasuwa.
Also reported missing from the same expedition was Mohd Sani Harul, the deputy director of operations at the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM).
Two days after the incident, Hani flew to Kathmandu on her own initiative to seek the latest information on the search and rescue operation. Today marks her sixth day in Nepal.
While there, she has shared updates on social media, including efforts to gather essential supplies for disaster victims. She has also sought permission to enter the affected areas to distribute aid.
Hani had previously expressed her wish to join a volunteer team travelling to camps housing survivors, in the hope of finding her husband.
Mohd Fakhrul Munir is among the Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the flash floods in Nepal, as efforts to locate the missing group continue.
A total of 55 Malaysians were reported uncontactable after the disaster on August 26. Another 77 Malaysians, who were confirmed safe in Tibet and Nepal, have been brought to Kathmandu for processing before returning to Malaysia.
Anadolu Agency reported that the disaster’s death toll had risen to 1,220, while 4,762 people, including 844 foreign nationals, remained missing. — Bernama

Title: Rising airfares could undermine Visit Sabah 2027 tourism push, says former state Matta chief
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 3 — The government should consider targeted assistance or subsidies to address rising airfares and fuel costs that could undermine Sabah’s tourism competitiveness ahead of Visit Sabah 2027, said former Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Sabah chairman Mohd Azlan Saleh Abd Salam.
He said high travel costs could prompt tourists to choose other destinations in the region offering more competitive prices, particularly as Sabah prepares to ramp up its tourism promotion.
“Based on indicative checks, the basic economy-class return fare from Kuala Lumpur to Kota Kinabalu is around RM471, while Kuala Lumpur-Jakarta is around RM487.
“This small difference is causing consumers to start comparing destinations that offer better value,” he said in a statement today.
Azlan said the issue deserved particular attention during school holidays, festive periods and peak travel seasons, when airfares are among the key factors influencing tourists’ choice of destination.
He said rising petrol and diesel costs were also putting pressure on tourism operators, including tour bus, van and boat operators.
“Operators cannot absorb rising operating costs indefinitely, and these costs may eventually be passed on to consumers through higher package prices.
“The government should consider targeted fuel assistance or subsidies for licensed tourism operators, particularly tour buses, vans and tourist boats,” he said.
He said any assistance should be implemented transparently and conditionally, with proper monitoring to ensure the benefits were passed on through more stable tourism package prices.
Azlan also warned that Sabah was competing not only with other destinations in Malaysia but also with Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam.
“Strong promotion needs to be supported by sufficient and affordable air connectivity. We must not allow the major investment in Visit Sabah 2027 to fall short of its intended results because tourists choose other destinations due to high travel costs,” he said.
Tourism is a major income earner and economic driver for Sabah, generating RM13.7 billion in 2024, equivalent to 12 per cent of the state’s economy, and supporting about 387,600 jobs, according to Azlan.
Azlan urged the government to continue engaging industry players and use actual tourism-sector data when formulating measures to address airfares and operating costs.
“Competition today is not only about the beauty of a destination, but also air connectivity, prices, facilities and the overall value offered to tourists.
“If the issues of airfares and fuel costs are addressed promptly, Visit Sabah 2027 could become an important catalyst for the state’s economic growth,” he said.
Domestic travel also hurting
Aside from tourism, high airfares are also increasingly affecting Sabahans and other Malaysians travelling between Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.
Sabah Youth, Sports Development and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan was recently reported as saying that the state government was seeking federal intervention following reports that one-way fares from Tawau to Kuala Lumpur had reached as much as RM1,000, particularly affecting students studying in the peninsula.
He urged the Transport Ministry to intervene and ensure students were not affected by exorbitant fares.
The impact of high airfares is also being felt by families who need to travel between Sabah and the peninsula for work and family commitments.
In June, it was reported that Md Suhaimi Sapiee, a 48-year-old commissioner for oaths, was unable to return to Selangor to attend his sister’s funeral because of the high cost of air travel.
He said airfares of more than RM1,000 per person also meant that only one of his two children studying in Peninsular Malaysia could return to Kota Kinabalu during their recent semester break.
Sabahans working in West Malaysia also often take to social media to lament the high cost of flights, which prevents them from returning home frequently during festive periods to see their families, while the reduced frequency of flights also means a potential loss of business for many.
Students who can utilise the FlySiswa subsidy programme say it helps ease the cost of flights to Kota Kinabalu, but their families may still be unable to visit them for graduation because of high airfares.
The combination of rising fares and operating costs has therefore emerged as an issue affecting both Sabah’s tourism ambitions and the ability of Sabahans to maintain regular links with Peninsular Malaysia.
For the tourism industry, Azlan said the challenge was to ensure that efforts to promote Sabah as a destination were matched by affordable and accessible air connectivity.

Title: Akmal Nasrullah: Oil and gas here to stay even as Malaysia pushes for green energy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Oil and gas will continue to play a critical role in supporting Malaysia’s economic growth and safeguarding national energy security, even as the country accelerates its shift toward cleaner energy sources, Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
Speaking at the Oil and Gas Asia Convention, Akmal emphasised that natural gas will remain a major component of Malaysia’s primary energy mix through 2050.
“It is, in particular, a key transitional fuel that supports power generation, industry, and system reliability as renewables scale up, enabling higher renewable penetration while ensuring stability,” Akmal told attendees during a panel session at the event.
Malaysia currently has a relatively diversified energy mix, with natural gas accounting for 42 per cent of total primary energy supply in 2024, followed by crude oil and petroleum products at 33 per cent, coal and coke at 22 per cent, and hydropower and renewables at 4 per cent.
The Anwar administration launched the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) a year after taking power, one of its hallmark policies that is said was designed to accelerate the country’s shift toward clean energy as part of Malaysia’s broader diversification push to secure its energy supply.
Akmal said the plan clearly outlines targeted investments and key flagship projects across areas like renewable energy, hydrogen, energy storage, and natural gas infrastructure through 2050, and the government would commit more investment in gas-related infrastructure.
Still, the minister cautioned against relying too heavily on any single energy source. Despite being oil and gas rich, Malaysia was still exposed to supply risks and market disruptions that followed the war in the Middle East.
“Excessive dependence on any single source creates vulnerability,” Akmal said.
“The objective is not simply to replace one energy source with another. It is to give Malaysia more options, reduce exposure to external shocks, and create new sources of economic value,” he added.
Most domestic gas is produced offshore in Sabah and Sarawak and exported primarily to East Asia.
Peninsular Malaysia, which consumes the majority of energy, uses regasification terminals in Malacca and Pengerang to import LNG primarily from Australia, Brunei, and the US alongside pipeline imports from Indonesia to meet domestic energy needs.

Title: Malaysia must act now as 10pc US tariff not guaranteed ceiling, says industry expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Malaysia should not regard the 10 per cent tariff currently imposed by the United States on its goods as a guaranteed ceiling, as Washington could review the rate if it is dissatisfied with the country’s efforts to address its concerns, said industry practitioner Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan.
He said while the 10 per cent rate offered some relief to Malaysian businesses compared with potentially higher tariffs, exporters should remain cautious as the US could take further action depending on the outcome of its investigations.
“Businesses should understand that 10 per cent is not a guaranteed ceiling. If the US is not satisfied with Malaysia’s response or believes that the commitments made are not being properly implemented, there is a possibility that further measures could be considered,” he said in a statement today.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of maritime experience, said the issue was particularly important given the ongoing US investigation into structural excess capacity involving Malaysia and several other economies.
Recently, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the US was expected to announce its findings from the excess capacity investigation involving Malaysia within three to four weeks.
Johari said the current 10 per cent tariff formed part of broader US action involving 60 economies under Section 301 of the Trade Act 1974, with Malaysia among 17 economies subjected to the lower tariff rate.
The remaining economies are subject to a 12.5 per cent tariff, he said.
Jeyenderan, who is also chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, said Malaysia should use the period before the US announces its findings to strengthen its evidence and demonstrate that its commitments were being effectively implemented.
He said US concerns over goods moving through third countries also made strong transshipment controls important to Malaysia’s defence in the investigation.
“Yes, in my view. Weak records would make it harder to distinguish genuine Malaysian production from goods merely passing through. That would undermine credibility, although it would not itself prove excess capacity,” he said.
Jeyenderan said Malaysia’s ability to trace goods through the supply chain was therefore critical in demonstrating that exports attributed to the country genuinely originated from Malaysian production.
“Our K8 concerns raise a related issue: can authorities reconcile the cargo that arrived, what happened during storage or any blending, and what ultimately left?
“Those are practical questions about traceability that deserve documented answers,” he said.
He said the most urgent step was for the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (MITI) and Customs Department to assemble verified industry data, audit cargo movements where risks were highest, and demonstrate effective enforcement of forced-labour import restrictions.
“For K8 petroleum cargo, the authorities should issue a clear written determination on permitted storage and blending, the correct declarations, and the resulting classification and tax treatment.
“Maritime Network has already sought clarification on these matters. Resolving them would give businesses certainty and strengthen Malaysia’s ability to defend its controls internationally,” he said.
Jeyenderan said a clear and documented position from the relevant authorities would also help reduce uncertainty among businesses involved in petroleum and maritime trade.
He said Malaysia should ensure that any weaknesses identified through the US investigation were addressed promptly and transparently, rather than waiting for further tariff measures to be imposed.
“Malaysia needs to demonstrate not only that the rules exist, but that they are being properly implemented, monitored and enforced,” he said.

Title: Ipoh police probe viral video of two children sitting on roof of moving MPV
Article:
IPOH, Sept 3 — Police are investigating a viral video showing two children sitting on the roof of a moving multi-purpose vehicle (MPV),
Astro Awani
eported.
Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police had yet to receive any report regarding the incident.
However, he said police were tracing the owner of the vehicle.
“We will identify [the owner]. If they are indeed children, we will investigate the matter under the Child Act 2001,” he was quoted as saying when contacted.
The video, which went viral on social media yesterday, showed two girls sitting on the roof of a luxury Toyota Alphard MPV.
The children were believed to have climbed out through the vehicle’s sunroof while it was moving along the road.
The incident was believed to have taken place from the Meru exit towards Jalan Jelapang-Simpang Pulai, alongside the North-South Expressway.
The recording, taken by a passing motorist, drew criticism from netizens over the potential danger posed to the children.

Title: Search continues for two more after second teen confirmed drowned in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The body of one of the three teenagers who went missing while bathing at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Kota Tinggi was found at 1.53 pm today.
Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime headquarters operations officer Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, 16, was found floating about 800 metres from the location where the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, was found yesterday.
He said the victim’s body was safely brought to the shore at around 2.50 pm this afternoon and was confirmed dead by health officials.
“The family has also been identified and confirmed that the body is that of the victim who went missing yesterday,” he said at a press conference at the scene of the incident, here today.
He said the victim’s body has been taken for a post-mortem at the Kota Tinggi Hospital.
He said the search for Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal and Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian, both 16 years old, was ongoing, with a search radius of seven nautical miles from the northwest of the beach.
“The search with the other agencies will continue until the victim is found,” he said.
Yesterday, Kota Tinggi deputy district police chief DSP Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad was reported to have said that the body of the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin, was found about 500 metres from the location where he was reported missing.
Fire and Rescue Service Department announced that it received an emergency call at 8.19 am regarding the incident, with six 16-year-old victims being part of a group of 15 people who had come to camp in the area for the past two days.
However, two of them were successfully rescued by the public, while the other four were missing and feared drowned. — Bernama

Title: Law minister: Coroners Bill to be tabled next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Coroners Bill, aimed at clarifying the management of death cases, is expected to be tabled in Parliament next year, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the bill was originally targeted for tabling this year, but with the Budget 2027 session in October, it is more suitable to bring it next year.
Azalina said drafting the law is expected to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and detail the roles of coroners and relevant parties in handling death cases.
“We hope that with this act, we can establish SOPs and answer questions that arise. We do not want families searching for answers when a death occurs,” she told reporters after launching the Public Opinion Survey on the Drafting of the Coroners Bill here today.
Azalina said, although procedures for death investigations exist under current legislation, the Coroners Act will complement them and offer clearer guidance on implementation.
Earlier in her speech, Azalina said specific legislation on coroners is being considered with three main goals: establishing a clear and comprehensive legal framework; creating a more structured, independent and transparent coroner system; and clarifying each party’s responsibilities when a death is reported.
“We also want a system that not only determines the cause of death but also identifies weaknesses to prevent similar tragedies from recurring.
“If a death reveals weaknesses in the system, the coroner’s findings should not end up buried in a file because the lessons learned from a case should help us protect other lives,” she said.
Azalina added that Malaysia currently has an inquest implementation framework under the Criminal Procedure Code, specifically Sections 328 to 341A, as well as Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.
However, she said that death investigations have become more complex, involving digital evidence, forensic analysis, medical records, institutional safety, and inter-agency coordination.
Azalina said that the ongoing inquest proceedings into the death of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir serve as a reminder of the importance of evidence management, post-mortems, inter-agency coordination, and early communication with families.
She also cited the cases of the late Muhammad Adib Mohd Kassim and the late Teoh Beng Hock, as well as custodial deaths such as those of the late A. Kugan and the late S. Balamurugan, as reminders of the need for an independent, thorough, and credible process when serious questions arise surrounding a death.
She said the need for this legal reform had also been raised by the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (SUHAKAM), the Malaysian Bar, the Tun Dzaiddin Royal Commission Report, and the Royal Commission of Inquiry into the death of Teoh Beng Hock.
“The principle is simple: justice should not depend on whether a case goes viral. Every death that must be reported deserves the same scrutiny, whether it catches nationwide attention or is mourned by a single family,” she said.
Meanwhile, Azalina said the government is examining a proposal to establish a Law Reform Commission as a permanent, dedicated, and structured mechanism to review national laws and systematically submit reform recommendations on an ongoing, independent, and evidence-based basis.
She stressed that law reform need not be ad hoc or driven solely by crises but should be executed in a planned way to ensure the national legal framework remains relevant and responsive to current social needs. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: PM term limit and AG/PP separation Bills ready for Parliament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A Bill to limit the tenure of the prime minister is ready for its second reading in the Dewan Rakyat, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
However, she said the decision on whether to table the Bill at the next parliamentary sitting rested with the Leader of the House, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“Everything is ready. The limit on the prime minister’s term is ready. It is subject to the Leader of the House, the Prime Minister, on whether we want to bring it for a vote at the next sitting,” she told reporters after launching the Public Opinion Survey on the Drafting of the Coroners Bill here today.
Azalina said the proposed term limit for the prime minister would involve amendments to the Federal Constitution and would therefore require the support of a two-thirds majority in Parliament.
She said the same applied to the Bill on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General (AG) and Public Prosecutor (PP), which would also require a two-thirds majority.
“Since both Bills involve amendments to the Federal Constitution, we need a two-thirds majority. The same applies to the separation of the roles of the AG and PP, which also requires a two-thirds majority. So, domestic politics does play a role,” she said.
In this regard, Azalina appealed to all members of parliament, regardless of political affiliation, to support the proposed reforms, saying they could help reduce perceptions of politically motivated prosecutions.
“I sincerely hope that members of the Dewan Rakyat, the Dewan Negara and all political parties will welcome these Bills because they bring more benefits than drawbacks. This is for our country,” she said.
At the same time, Azalina said the Bill separating the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor was also expected to strengthen confidence in the country’s prosecution system.
“I do not want to hear people claiming, whenever they are charged, that there is some hidden agenda behind it.
“
InsyaAllah
, this separation of roles will inspire greater confidence, especially when the Public Prosecutor is appointed through a parliamentary process,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji Act amendments in final stages before parliamentary tabling, says TH CEO
Article:
BANGI, Sept 3 — The process of amending the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) has now reached 90 per cent at the internal level of the Tabung Haji Board (TH) and is expected to be brought to the Cabinet after the technical process and engagement with relevant parties are finalised.
TH chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the amendment was among the remaining main actions following the 25 recommendations submitted by the TH Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
"One of the most important is the amendment to Act 535. This is still in our (action), I can tell you that we are more than 90 per cent in action.
"But there needs to be an end for us to bring to the Cabinet, a policy change that we need to bring to the Cabinet and to Parliament later," he said at the Dialog Ummah: Reality and Future of TH programme here today.
Mustakim said that currently, 19 out of 25 recommendations of the TH RCI, which is about 76 per cent, have been completed while the remaining six are still in action at all levels.
The remaining six actions include amendments to Act 535; limiting the scope of Bank Negara Malaysia's supervision of TH and strengthening the disciplinary process.
Meanwhile, TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain said his party has been working on the amendment intensively for the past year, including holding engagement sessions with relevant regulatory bodies.
Asked about the timeframe for the amendment to be tabled, he said the process of amending the Act need to go through several stages including the consideration of ministers, the Cabinet and the Attorney General's Department before being brought to Parliament.
"It will have to go through the process with the AG's Office for the final opinion. That's the process, and I will go through that process,” he said in a separate press conference.
Previously, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post that the government would implement amendments to Act 535 to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be preserved.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said the amendments were among the steps taken by the MADANI Government in strengthening governance and ensuring that every institutional weakness is firmly corrected.
Following that, TH welcomed the government's move to amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995 in line with the RCI's recommendations to strengthen governance in ensuring that the trust entrusted to it continues to be preserved.
TH announced that as an Islamic financial institution that manages the savings of Muslims to perform the hajj, TH is committed to continuing to strengthen governance, transparency and integrity in order to safeguard the interests of depositors and the sustainability of the institution. — Bernama

Title: Senior Citizens Bill delayed to early 2027, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 3 — The Senior Citizens Bill, previously targeted for tabling this October, is expected to be brought to Parliament in early 2027.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said that although the draft bill is complete, the process is taking time due to engagement sessions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and state governments.
“Our timeline was indeed this year. However, we were informed that after the engagement sessions, many new elements need to be incorporated, and we agreed to include them as amendments to our draft,” she told reporters after attending the Social Welfare Department’s 80th Anniversary celebration here today.
Nancy said the next step involves further scrutiny before the bill can be finalised and submitted to the next stage.
The new law aims to provide more comprehensive legal protection, particularly in addressing issues of neglect, abuse, and exploitation involving senior citizens.
Additionally, the legislation is part of comprehensive preparations for Malaysia’s demographic transition to becoming an ageing nation by 2028. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: Tech advances require modern laws to combat crime
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Rapid technological advances have reshaped the crime landscape, underscoring the need to strengthen laws, enforcement capabilities and strategic cooperation to safeguard public security in both the physical and digital worlds.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the increasingly complex challenges required the government and enforcement agencies to adopt a comprehensive approach involving multiple stakeholders.
“For the Home Ministry, these challenges require us to strengthen our laws, enforcement capabilities and strategic cooperation to ensure that the safety of the people continues to be safeguarded, whether in the physical or digital world,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said the government and enforcement agencies could not face increasingly complex threats alone, but must instead harness the strengths of various sectors through a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach.
“Increasingly complex threats require a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach, bringing together the strengths of the government, enforcement agencies, academia, industry, technology providers and international partners,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution said the academic community and researchers had an important role in ensuring that security-related research findings were translated into action that benefited the public.
“Research should not end as publications or discussions at conferences. Knowledge and research findings must be translated into policies, strengthen enforcement capabilities and produce solutions to the real security challenges faced by the people,” he said.
Meanwhile, he congratulated the organisers and participants of the Sixth International Cyber Resilience Conference (CRC2026), which he said played an important role in bridging research, policymaking, enforcement and national security needs.
“CRC2026 must therefore serve as a bridge between research and policy, knowledge and enforcement, as well as expertise and the needs of the nation,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution also challenged academics and researchers to ensure that their findings did not stop at conference discussions, but were translated into policies, action and protective measures that had a tangible impact on the people.
The three-day CRC2026, which began on Tuesday in Bangi, brings together expertise and perspectives on cyber resilience amid evolving digital security threats. — Bernama

Title: DOE samples factory discharge after dead fish and crabs found in Sungai Sitiawan
Article:
IPOH, Sept 3 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has collected industrial effluent samples from a manufacturing factory as part of its investigation into alleged river pollution after fish and crabs were found dead in Sungai Sitiawan.
The department said the samples were taken at the premises’ final discharge point to allow investigators to compare them with water samples collected from the river.
“Industrial effluent samples were taken at the final discharge point of the premises. This is to enable the matching of samples from the premises with the river water samples,” it said in a statement today.
During an inspection of the factory, the DOE said its investigation team identified a malfunction involving a blower valve at the factory’s Sewage Treatment Plant (STP).
However, sewage effluent samples could not be collected as the flow rate at the time was very low, at 0.583 cubic metres per hour, it said.
The DOE said it received information about dead fish being discovered in Sungai Sitiawan at 9.57am on Aug 30.
Investigations were subsequently carried out at three locations — Wak Dol Jetty, D’ Chalet accommodation and Tanjung Uda River Resort.
“At the complaint locations, several fish and other aquatic life were found dead and floating on the surface,” the DOE said.
It said small fish were found at Wak Dol Jetty, while larger fish were found dead at the D’ Chalet location.
The department also conducted in-situ testing and collected water samples from all three locations for further analysis by the Chemistry Department Malaysia.
The in-situ tests recorded dissolved oxygen readings of 5.86mg/L at Wak Dol Jetty, 3.79mg/L at D’ Chalet and 1.59mg/L at Tanjung Uda River Resort.
The DOE said it would await the analysis of the river water and industrial effluent samples by the Chemistry Department Malaysia before determining further action.
“Legal action will follow depending on the results of the analysis of the samples by the Chemistry Department Malaysia,” it said.
The department added that it would continue monitoring the situation and conduct enforcement inspections on nearby premises that could potentially be responsible for polluting the river.

Title: Penang gazettes Hungry Ghost Festival as state heritage, six sites also set for official recognition
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang has gazetted the Teong Guan Phor Thor, or Hungry Ghost Festival, as a state heritage item under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011, recognising a traditional celebration observed by more than 200 groups across the state.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government approved its nomination on April 8, before it came into force as Penang heritage on June 25.
The Hungry Ghost Festival is observed during the seventh month of the Chinese lunar calendar, when Buddhists and Taoists conduct rituals to honour ancestors and spirits believed to roam during the period.
The festival also involves local communities and traders setting up Tai Su Yeah, or King of Hell, tents and opera or
getai
stages in public spaces.
“Recognition is not merely to preserve and conserve a traditional practice, but also to elevate the diversity of celebrations in our multiracial society as part of Penang’s identity,” Chow said at a press conference in his office in Komtar here.
He said the nomination was screened by the state’s Intangible Cultural Heritage (Sociocultural) Expert Committee, endorsed by the State Heritage Council and approved by the state executive council.
The state also approved the designation of six heritage sites on April 8, Chow said.
Their gazette notices have been submitted to the state legal adviser’s office for official gazettement.
The upper and lower stations and funicular railway line of Penang Hill have been gazetted as a state heritage site.
The sites are the upper and lower stations and funicular railway line of Penang Hill; Dato Koyah’s tomb; Thai Pak Koong Temple (Ng Suk) on King Street; the Fooi Chew Association building; Loo Pun Hong Temple; and Kwangtung and Tengchow Cemetery No. 1.
“The gazettement of the six sites and Hungry Ghost Festival will be officiated on October 10,” Chow said.
State tourism and creative economy executive councillor Wong Hon Wai said the seven newly announced items — one intangible heritage item and six sites — were in addition to 50 heritage items announced earlier this year.
The earlier list comprised 15 heritage sites, 28 food heritage items and seven intangible heritage items.
“This year is a productive year for heritage,” he said.
He added that the 57 items cover the state’s cultural diversity on both Penang island and the mainland.
State Heritage Commissioner Zalena Abdul Aziz said the office hoped to bring the total number of announced heritage items to at least 70 next year, in conjunction with Malaysia’s 70th independence anniversary.
Chow said nominations could originate from the state heritage commissioner’s office, or from owners, associations and practitioners who believe a site or practice merits recognition.
He added that selected state-listed items could subsequently be proposed for consideration under the National Heritage Act, while other efforts could eventually extend to Unesco recognition.
Among the other intangible cultural heritage recognised earlier this year are nasi kandar culture, kopitiam culture, the Thaipusam procession, the Chingay procession, the St Anne’s Feast in Bukit Mertajam, and the Tanjong Penang Malay dialect.
The state has also gazetted traditional foods as state heritage, including
nasi kandar
,
pasembor
,
char kue kak,
oh chien
,
kerabu bihun, mi hokkien, mi udang, mi sotong, mi jawa
and
roti benggali.

Title: Court of Appeal sets aside fraud, conspiracy findings in RM52.2m Johor land dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Court of Appeal has set aside findings of fraud and conspiracy against a businessman and property agent in a dispute over a proposed RM52.2 million sale of a 22ha tract of land in Johor.
However, a three-member panel upheld the High Court’s findings that no binding sale agreement had been concluded and that businessman J. Siva Kumar had wrongfully lodged a private caveat over the land.
The panel comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Shahid and Datuk Ong Chee Kwan delivered its decision in two consolidated appeals arising from the High Court’s judgment dated January 22, 2024.
The first appeal was brought by Siva and Ammsa Property Sdn Bhd, while the second was filed by property agent R Thevandran K. Ragavan, also known as Thevan.
The dispute concerns a 22.06ha agricultural tract held under Lot 49259, Geran 5238, Mukim Plentong, Johor Bahru, owned by Firwas Sdn Bhd.
Siva and Ammsa had sought specific performance of an alleged sale and purchase agreement with Firwas.
In its decision, the Court of Appeal held that the High Court had gone beyond Firwas’ pleaded case when it made findings of fraud and conspiracy against Siva, Thevan and lawyer G Shoba without those causes of action and their constituent facts having been pleaded with the required particularity.
The appellate court therefore set aside the findings of fraud and conspiracy and overturned the High Court’s declaration that the alleged sale and purchase agreement was “illegal, fraudulent, void ab initio”.
The court nevertheless held that the agreement remained unenforceable as there had been no concluded agreement between Siva and Firwas, nor any binding authority on Firwas’ part to enter into such an agreement.
It also upheld the finding that Siva had wrongfully lodged the private caveat over the land.
The court rejected Siva’s argument that an earlier High Court decision dismissing Firwas’ application to remove the caveat prevented a subsequent finding that it had been wrongfully lodged.
The Court of Appeal held that the earlier proceedings were interlocutory in nature and had not determined the parties’ substantive rights at trial.
On damages, the court allowed Firwas’ cross-appeal and ordered interest on the RM52.2 million sum to be recalculated at eight per cent per annum from September 22, 2020 until the date of judgment.
Siva and Ammsa were also ordered to pay RM80,000 in costs for their appeal.
Meanwhile, Thevan’s appeal over his claim for RM1.2 million in agency fees was dismissed.
Although the findings of fraud and conspiracy against Thevan were set aside, the Court of Appeal upheld his liability for breach of fiduciary duty.
The court ordered him to pay RM100,000 in aggravated damages and for the RM1.2 million earnest deposit he had retained to be paid to Firwas towards satisfaction of the judgment debt.
Shoba, who did not appeal, remains liable for breach of fiduciary duty as a partner of the law firm involved in the transaction.
The case dates back to negotiations in 2017 and 2018, when Firwas sought to sell the Johor land for RM60 million.
Thevan had introduced Siva as a prospective purchaser. The negotiations eventually broke down and Firwas sold the land to another party for RM58 million.
Siva subsequently proceeded with an alleged sale agreement and lodged a private caveat over the property, leading Firwas to take legal action.
The High Court had ruled in favour of Firwas in January 2024, making strong findings of fraud and conspiracy and awarding damages over the wrongful caveat.
The Court of Appeal’s latest decision removes those fraud and conspiracy findings but leaves intact the key finding that there was no binding sale agreement and that Siva’s caveat was wrongful.

Title: SAR area expanded to two nautical miles in search for three missing teenagers in Tanjung Lompat
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three teenagers missing at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar has been expanded to cover up to two nautical miles of coastal waters today.
Tanjung Sedili Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) acting director Mohd Najib Sam said the search area was widened following the discovery of one victim about 500 metres from the incident site yesterday.
“Today’s SAR operational area has been increased from one to two nautical miles of coastal area in an effort to locate the three missing teenagers.
“The expanded area takes into account that there is a possibility that the missing teenagers are further away from their initial location,” he told reporters at the SAR command centre in Tanjung Lompat here today.
Mohd Najib said the operation resumed at 7am today involving 41 officers and personnel from various agencies, with two drones — one each from MMEA and the Fire and Rescue Department — deployed to assist the search.
He said the drones conducted two flights in the morning and would continue operating during high tide to determine whether the missing teenagers had been swept towards other nearby coastal areas.
“The drones flew two sessions in the morning in an effort to locate the missing victims.
“The drones will continue to be flown during high tide to see if the victims were washed away to other nearby coastal areas,” he said.
Mohd Najib said rough weather was also hampering the operation, with waves reaching 1.15 metres.
“The situation may change again in the afternoon due to the expected high tide and bad weather,” he said.
He added that authorities in neighbouring countries had been informed of the incident through the Maritime Rescue Sub-Centre (MRSC) in Johor Bahru.
However, he said the SAR operation remained focused on Malaysian waters, including onshore areas.
It was reported yesterday that four teenage boys were feared to have drowned after a beach outing, while two others were rescued.
The body of the first victim, Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, 16, was found by the SAR team with the assistance of villagers at 1.25pm yesterday, about 800 metres from where he was last seen.
The three teenagers still missing are Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian and Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, all aged 16.

Title: Asyraf Wajdi says only Zahid can decide whether he should step down as Mara chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mara chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said only Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi could decide whether he should step down from the position.
Asyraf, who is also Umno secretary-general, said he would comply if Zahid asked him to resign, but stressed that he would not do so due to pressure from PKR’s youth wing Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) or the party.
“I was appointed by the Deputy Prime Minister, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister. I will simply follow his instructions.
“If the Rural and Regional Development Minister asks me to step down, I will step down — but not because of pressure from AMK or Parti Keadilan,” he told reporters during a special press conference ahead of the Umno General Assembly at Menara Dato Onn here.
Asyraf said his priority was to safeguard Mara, which he described as an institution entrusted with the interests of Malays and Bumiputeras and established under Umno’s leadership.
“First and foremost, I am safeguarding the party’s trust and mandate — the party’s mandate to protect Mara, which was born from the same womb of Umno itself.
“This is an institution for the Malays and Bumiputeras, and over the past three years, I have laid important foundations to ensure that the educational and Malay entrepreneurship agendas are preserved and strengthened,” he said.
Asyraf said Mara’s reputation and role as a Malay and Bumiputera institution must be protected from efforts to undermine it.
“What is most important is that this institution continues to be protected. There must not be efforts to tear down its reputation, nor should there be external elements deliberately seeking to see this Malay institution fall,” he said.
He said he would continue defending Mara if there were attempts to undermine the institution.
“This is not about Asyraf Wajdi. This is about Mara as an institution entrusted with the interests of the Malays, which was entrusted to Umno’s leadership when Mara was established in 1964 at the Umno General Assembly.
“So, I believe the only person who is rightfully in a position to decide whether I should step down or not is the Deputy Prime Minister, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister and oversees Mara as an agency under the ministry,” he said.
On calls for him to resign over the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji, Asyraf said the matter was irrelevant as his name was not mentioned in the inquiry.
“The Tabung Haji RCI is not relevant because my name was not mentioned in the Tabung Haji RCI, nor have I ever been linked to issues involving Tabung Haji and so on.
“This is merely a matter of perception being played up by those who want to undermine the reputation and image of this institution,” he said.

Title: Umno’s future direction, unity govt ties among key issues at upcoming general assembly, says Asyraf Wajdi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Umno’s direction and its political cooperation within the unity government are expected to be among the key issues debated at the party’s upcoming general assembly, with motions received from all 157 divisions.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said political cooperation, particularly within the framework of the unity government, and the Rumah Bangsa agenda proposed at the previous Umno General Assembly were the two most popular issues raised by the divisions.
“The main motions include the issue of Umno’s direction and political cooperation, particularly within the framework of the unity government, as well as the Rumah Bangsa agenda proposed at the previous Umno General Assembly.
“These are the two most popular issues raised by the divisions,” he told reporters at a special press conference ahead of the Umno General Assembly at Menara Dato Onn here today.
Asyraf said the party would not restrict delegates from debating any issue, including topics that had generated discussion on social media.
“We will never restrict delegates from debating whatever they wish. Looking at the sentiments on social media, these are indeed among the hot topics.
“But I do not want to pre-empt the Umno General Assembly. We are open to any debate by the delegates,” he said.
He said the assembly should serve as a platform for delegates, including those from Umno’s three wings — Wanita, Pemuda and Puteri — to discuss the party’s future direction openly and thoroughly.
“Most importantly, we should make the most of this Umno General Assembly, including the assemblies of the wings, to discuss openly and thoroughly the direction of the party towards a better future for the people and the country,” he said.
On the party’s direction, Asyraf said the matter encompassed various important aspects of Umno’s struggle and should be left to delegates to debate at the assembly.
He said the Umno General Assembly remained the party’s highest platform to determine its policies and direction.
“If the Umno General Assembly decides on anything, the leadership must accept and follow it,” he said.
Asyraf also said 6,401 delegates would attend this year’s Umno General Assembly.
He expects more than 50,000 people to attend the four-day event at the Putra World Trade Centre (PWTC) from Sept 9 to 12.
“We expect a large turnout at PWTC this time. I expect more than 50,000 people to attend over the four days, as we have received a very large number of requests and applications to attend over the past two months,” he said.

Title: Penang eyes record manufacturing investments after RM17.3b secured in first half
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang is optimistic it will surpass last year’s RM22.4 billion in approved manufacturing investments after securing RM17.3 billion in the first half of 2026, with several projects yet to be reflected in the latest figures.
InvestPenang chief executive officer Datuk Seri Loo Lee Lian said the additional projects were not included in figures released by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) last week.
“We have a few more projects that haven’t been included in the figure, so once [they are] included, we hope to achieve more than last year,” she said at a press conference with Penang chief minister Chow Kon Yeow in Komtar today.
Chow attributed the outlook partly to the artificial intelligence (AI) supercycle, which he said had benefited Penang and other South-east Asian economies.
“Penang’s RM17.3 billion in approved manufacturing investments from January to June represented a 38 per cent increase from the corresponding period last year,” he said.
The figure accounted for 34 per cent of Malaysia’s total approved manufacturing investments, he said.
Chow said the state had continued to receive enquiries and requests for additional land from existing companies seeking to expand.
Expansion projects made up RM11.9 billion, or 69 per cent, of the total approved investments, while new projects accounted for RM5.4 billion, he said.
“It is not only new foreign direct investment and new domestic direct investment, but expansion of existing operations as well,” he said.
The approved investments cover 177 projects and are expected to create 19,337 jobs.
Foreign direct investment amounted to RM12.8 billion, or 74 per cent of the total, while domestic direct investment reached RM4.5 billion, up 125 per cent year-on-year.
Chow said the figures should encourage small and medium enterprises to pursue opportunities in the state’s large industrial ecosystem and supply chain.
He said the impact of current approved investments would likely be felt over the next 18 to 24 months, after plants are built, equipped, staffed and begin operating.
“Penang has consistently recorded good results over the years,” Chow said.
He added that the state was equally optimistic that the AI boom would continue drawing investments into Malaysia and Penang.

Title: Sultan Ibrahim meets Singapore FM at Istana Pasir Pelangi in Johor Bahru
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 3 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today granted an audience to Singaporean Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan today.
According to Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook post, the audience took place at Pavilion 2 of Istana Pasir Pelangi Polo Grounds, here.
Also present were Singapore’s High Commissioner to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon and Consul-General in Johor Bahru Ng Kuan Hai. — Bernama

Title: Zairil accuses Hadi of using religious sentiment to deflect Tabung Haji scrutiny
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang DAP vice-chairman Zairil Khir Johari today accused PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang of using religious sentiment to divert attention from alleged governance and integrity failures at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Zairil said Hadi’s alleged description of the issue as an “attack on Islamic identity” was an attempt to deflect scrutiny from the institution’s management.
“Using religious sentiment as a shield to defend weaknesses or wrongdoing not only confuses the public, but also diminishes the dignity of Islamic institutions,” he said in a statement today.
He also questioned Hadi’s silence when alleged wrongdoing at TH was disclosed through the Royal Commission of Inquiry report last month.
“It is hypocritical to remain silent when the crisis occurred, but to speak loudly when corrective action is taken,” Zairil said.
He further criticised PAS and Perikatan Nasional MPs for allegedly walking out and boycotting a parliamentary motion related to TH instead of debating the matter.
Zairil said the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s detention and remand of former TH leaders, including a former religious affairs minister, showed that the matter was not a “narrow political motive” but a case requiring accountability.
“Tabung Haji is not merely a financial body. It carries the trust and hopes of millions of Muslims,” he said.
“Every ringgit in it comes from the hard work, sacrifices and years of savings of ordinary people who aspire to perform the haj.
“TH must be fully cleansed of any wrongdoing and political manipulation, while the people’s trust must be upheld through transparent, firm and accountable governance.”

Title: ‘Malaysia, Jom Check!’: Free health screenings for STR recipients aged 40 and up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — ProtectHealth Corporation Sdn Bhd (ProtectHealth) under the Ministry of Health (MOH) is offering free health screening services to eligible Malaysians through the PeKa B40 2026 Programme in conjunction with the ‘Malaysia, Jom Check!’ campaign.
ProtectHealth in a statement today announced that the community health screening programme nationwide on Sept 5 to 6 aims to provide Malaysians with an opportunity to check their health status.
According to ProtectHealth, the PeKa B40 2026 Programme is also being implemented to encourage the public to undergo regular health screenings to detect high blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol problems at an early stage before they become more serious.
“Among the screenings that will be provided are blood pressure, height and weight measurements, blood sample collection and consultation with a doctor.
“This programme is especially encouraged for recipients of the 2026 Sumbang Tunai Rahmah (STR) who are aged 40 and above or registered spouses of STR recipients who are aged 40 and above, however PeKa B40 recipients are automatically eligible to attend this programme,” according to the statement.
The statement also informed that the programme will be held at selected locations in the states of Selangor, Pahang, Johor, Kelantan, Terengganu, Penang, Kedah, Perlis, Perak, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Sabah and Sarawak.
Eligible recipients are only required to bring their Identity Card (MyKad) as a simple step to check their eligibility, and no registration or fasting is required before attending the screening.
Malaysians who are unsure whether or not they are eligible to participate in the programme are advised to visit https://kelayakan.pekab40.com.my/semakan-kelayakan.
For more information or any enquiries regarding Malaysia, Jom Check! X PeKa B40 2026, please contact info@protecthealth.com.my via email or visit www.pekab40.com.my. — Bernama

Title: Former Tabung Haji COO’s corruption charges postponed after hospitalisation
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 3 — The reading of corruption charges against former Lembaga Tabung Haji chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani, who was scheduled to be charged today, was postponed after he was hospitalised for a heart problem.
Adi Azuan, 56, was initially scheduled to appear before the Sessions Court here to face several charges under Section 165 of the Penal Code.
Section 165 covers the offence of a public servant obtaining a valuable item without consideration.
When the case was called this morning, his lawyer Wan Azman Aiman Wan Fakhruddin informed Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud that his client had been hospitalised since Aug 31.
The lawyer said Adi Azuan was currently admitted to Universiti Malaya Medical Centre, where he had been undergoing a series of electrocardiogram tests.
Deputy public prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin appeared for the prosecution.
Adi Azuan’s wife, who was present in court, was later asked to explain her husband’s current condition but said she could not determine how long he would remain hospitalised.
She added that he was expected to undergo an angiogram as soon as possible, according to a doctor’s note submitted to the court by counsel earlier.
Awang Kerisnada later said the court accepted the accused’s wife’s explanation and agreed to postpone today’s hearing to a later date.
“At the moment it is not feasible to read the charge even at the hospital and we should let the accused person rest,” he said.
The case has been fixed for mention on Sept 24.
The Royal Commission of Inquiry report on Tabung Haji previously identified Adi Azuan among five senior officers subjected to disciplinary proceedings, noting that an initial proposal to dismiss four of them was later revised to demotions.

Title: TH Properties unit ex-manager hit with three CBT charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A former Health and Safety Manager of THP Bina Sdn Bhd was charged in the Sessions Court here today with three counts of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM72,000 in penalty funds collected in connection with a proposed office complex development project in Putrajaya.
Nasahruddin Ahmad, 56, pleaded not guilty to all the charges, which were read out separately before Judge Rosli Ahmad.
THP Bina is a wholly owned subsidiary of TH Properties Sdn Bhd, which in turn is a subsidiary of Lembaga Tabung Haji. The company specialises in construction and project management.
According to the charges, Nasahruddin, having been entrusted with RM72,000 collected as penalties from contractor Fourth Wave Sdn Bhd in his capacity as the company’s Health and Safety Manager, allegedly committed criminal breach of trust by depositing the funds into his personal account.
The penalty funds were related to a proposed office complex development in Precinct 3, Putrajaya, comprising: PT 12081 (Block A – 10-storey office, Block B – 9-storey office, an auditorium, and three levels of basement parking); PT 12075 (Block C – 7-storey office and two levels of basement parking); and PT 12074 (Block D – 9-storey office and two levels of basement parking).
The offences were allegedly committed at the Putrajaya Islamic Complex in Precinct 3 between April 26, 2013, and Aug 12, 2015.
The charges were brought under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment, whipping and a fine upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Haze drives up demand for bottled water, health products in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 3 — The haze has driven up demand for bottled water and health-related products at supermarkets here, with some retailers increasing their stock levels to meet customer needs.
At Farley Kuching, drinks department supervisor Nelson Ting, 23, said bottled water was selling faster than usual since the haze began.
“So far, I have noticed that the stock is moving quickly. We restock bottled water twice a week, as we normally do, but the quantity has increased due to the haze.
“For example, on normal days, the first delivery may consist of 50 cartons and the second 30 cartons. During the haze, we may receive 50 cartons for both deliveries,” he told
The Borneo Post.
Despite the increase in demand, Ting said the supermarket had not experienced any shortage of bottled water so far.
“Farley still has sufficient stock and there is no problem with the supply. We have increased the quantity compared with normal months, especially for August and September.
“The price also remains the same. There has been no price increase because of the haze,” he added.
He said customers were also showing greater interest in beverages believed to have cooling properties.
“This includes coconut water from brands like ‘Yeos’, cooling water (also well known as Cap Kaki Tiga), coconut juice, and Wang Lao Ji, a canned Chinese herbal tea.
“We have placed these drinks in areas where customers can easily see them. Some customers come in and ask: ‘Now that there is haze, I want to find drinks that can help with the heat in my body’,” he said.
Apart from beverages, Ting said demand had also increased for certain health and protective products.
“The products that customers frequently look for during the haze include medicine and face masks. For medicine, it is Panadol. Customers also try to find fruits such as watermelons,” he said.
He also advised members of the public to take precautions and prioritise their health during the haze.
“We cannot do much about the haze itself, so we can only take care of ourselves and our health. Drink plenty of water, including plain water, and wear a mask.”
Meanwhile, Emart Batu Kawa branch division head of grocery Danny Lau Yu Chai, 45, said the supermarket had also recorded an increase in demand for bottled drinking water.
“We have noticed an increase in demand for bottled water and signs of low stock. Bottled water supplies are also being restocked between two and three times a week.
“There is no effect on the price, but the supply will be affected,” he said.
He shared that the supermarket expected its current stock to be sufficient for this month.
“Currently the stock is sufficient for September but if the prolonged dry conditions of El Nino continues and peaks in coming December, there is a great risk of a shortage of drinking water from the end of October onwards until December this year,” he said.
Lau also said the supermarket had recorded strong demand for health and protective products besides bottled water.
“We have great demand for face masks, vitamin C gummies, cough drops, Panadol and Cool Fever products. There is also an increase in demand for fruits like pears, oranges and watermelons, which the customers see as beneficial due to their vitamin C content,” he explained.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Sarawak’s Daily Haze Watch, four stations recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at 4pm yesterday, including Kuching (309). — The Borne Post

Title: PAS Youth wants party to defend all existing seats in future elections
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 3 — PAS Youth has passed a motion calling for the party to defend all its existing parliamentary and state seats in future elections, including when it cooperates with other parties,
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) reported.
PAS Youth information chief Khairul Nadzir Helmi Azhar said the motion, tabled by a Padang Terap delegate, was unanimously approved by more than 800 delegates at the wing’s annual muktamar.
He said it was among six motions approved by PAS Youth to be brought to the main PAS muktamar, which begins today.
“This is to preserve the trust and confidence of voters who elected PAS to represent them. It is also a core policy in seat negotiations with allies,” he was quoted as saying last night.
The motion comes amid speculation that PAS-led Perikatan Nasional (PN) could cooperate with Barisan Nasional (BN) in the next general election, particularly after their alliance resulted in a victory in the Aug 1 Negeri Sembilan polls.
However, official talks between the two coalitions have yet to begin, while it remains uncertain whether BN and PN will form a pact for the Melaka state election, which is due by February 2027.
